title: Repairing Brexit economic damage should be Burnham’s top priority, business chief says
content_c:
Repairing the economic damage of Brexit should be the top priority for Andy Burnham as he reconsiders Labour’s red lines on EU membership, the head of one of Britain’s leading business groups has said.
Shevaun Haviland, the director general of the British Chambers of Commerce (BCC), said she welcomed the prime minister reopening the Brexit battle lines despite the uncertainty it could create, arguing that the UK’s current trading relationship with the EU was bad for business.
“We do think it’s right, because of what we know from the evidence of how businesses feel it’s not working,” she said.
Highlighting the continuing economic hit from Brexit, Haviland said more than half of bosses surveyed by the business lobby group believed the deal negotiated by Boris Johnson’s government and enacted in 2021 was not helping them.
“We expected it to be very difficult at the beginning, when [companies] were getting used to the new rules, and then it would sort of get easier as it went to along. But actually, that has not happened,” she said.
Economists estimate the cost to the UK economy has been up to £240bn so far, with national income per head between 6% and 8% lower than it would have been had the UK not left the EU. The Office for Budget Responsibility estimates a long-term hit of about 4% of gross domestic product.
At Labour’s conference in Liverpool last month, Burnham said Brexit had done “more harm than good” as he pledged to reassess Britain’s relationship with the EU. He opened the door to options including fully rejoining the bloc, and this week he said failing to pursue a better deal with the EU would be a “major dereliction of duty”.
In an interview with the Guardian in Norwich alongside the head of the Norfolk Chambers of Commerce (NCC) chief executive, Nova Fairbanks, Haviland said the government had to take into account business frustrations with Brexit.
She said the BCC would also consult its 50,000 members, who collectively employ more than 6 million people across the UK, on a range of options for Britain’s relationship, including rejoining the EU.
“We are 10 years since the referendum,” Haviland said. “We would say the language of Brexit needs to move on. That’s gone. What businesses understand is what we had before and what we’ve got now.
“We’re apolitical, it’s not a political question. It is an economic question. So we are going to set out the options, from the where we are to the most extreme. And in consultation with our chambers, and our partners, we will see where people are.”
Fairbanks said it was clear that some Brexit-backing bosses recognised the economic damage. “It would be very interesting to see how many businesses that were very much pro-Brexit are still pro-Brexit, because I’ve certainly not heard any change of heart from those that were against Brexit. I think they are still very much: ‘We need to be closer to Europe.’”
Speaking on the sidelines of an NCC trade fair at the Norfolk Showground, the business leaders said companies were coming under growing pressure from rising energy prices and other effects of the war in the Middle East.
Haviland called on the chancellor, John Healey, to take bold action at this month’s budget to support firms despite concerns at the heart of government about the pressure on the public finances amid jitters in the bond market.
“This rumour about a sort of ‘steady as she goes’ budget, and ‘let’s not upset the apple cart’. Business don’t really want just a ‘steady as she goes’. They want to see some action that will relieve some of those costs that will drive that fly wheel [of the British economy],” she said.
“You can’t just trot along in a crouch position effectively. And surely the markets will be happy to see some spending cuts by the government, and some investment in private-sector growth?”
Haviland called for action on energy bills, business rates and taxes on employment to help companies recruit more young people. “In your energy bill, about 40% of your energy is actually energy. The other 60% is about tax. So the government can get some of that out,” she said.
“The big test for the chancellor is to put his money where his mouth is for business at the budget. Just showing that he genuinely believes that the wealth creators are the job creators – which is business.”

title: Thousands of German gamblers could sue for their money back
content_c:
German gamblers could claim losses back
October 15, 2026
A German court has followed the European Court of Justice in finding that gamblers can seek compensation from gambling companies if they lost money when online casinos and fruit machines were illegal in Germany.
The verdicts could have major consequences for gambling addicts, as thousands of people could potentially bring civil lawsuits against gambling companies.
A series of court decisions at regional, federal, and European level have found in favor of gamblers in the last year, beginning with the Higher Regional Court Stuttgart in September 2025, which agreed with a plaintiff in the state of Baden-Württemberg who sued the Malta-based online betting company Tipico Games.
The plaintiff lost around €10,000 ($11,200) between 2020 and 2022, but because online gambling was prohibited in Germany until 2021, the court found that operators had therefore received the winnings without legal basis and must return them.
Wins for the losers
Tipico Games then appealed to the Federal Court of Justice (BGH), the highest civil and criminal court in Germany. In an initial verbal hearing in mid-September this year, the court followed the principle of the plaintiffs' case on one key point: That gamblers have the right to claim back losses if the companies did not have a license in Germany at the time the losses were incurred. But a final decision on the case is only expected to be made in January 2027.
Online casinos and fruit machines were banned in Germany from 2008 to 2021, but several gambling operators were active in the country because they had gaming licenses in other EU countries.
In April this year, the European Court of Justice ruled that EU law does not preclude a member state from "prohibiting certain services," or from "attaching civil-law consequences to that prohibition." In other words, even if a gambling company has a legitimate license in one member state, that doesn't override national gambling laws elsewhere.
Thomas Dünchheim, a business lawyer at global law firm Greenberg Traurig who specializes in gambling law, said law firms were now gathering clients — sometimes trawling the internet with the help of AI tools — to prepare massive collective lawsuits. Dünchheim himself has people who have lost tens of thousands of euros come to him seeking representation.
"The pendulum is swinging more and more towards the consumer. It's a bit like in America — we're seeing a mass phenomenon like the Dieselgate lawsuits against VW," he told DW. "And there are lawyers who will collect all these little cases, bundle them, and then maybe even drive it forward with the help of a legal financing firm. It's a good business for all involved, and the ones that will have to pay are the gambling firms who operated unlawful gambling in Germany."
The dangers of online gambling
The decisions could bring a measure of help for addicts, as online gambling can be particularly dangerous for people with addiction issues. According to Tobias Hayer, a psychologist at the Institute for Public Health and Nursing Research at Bremen University, that comes down to four main features of online gambling: Anonymity and the consequent lack of social control, 24/7 accessibility, the frictionless nature of cashless transactions, and the high frequency of games played.
"These court verdicts are not surprising at all," Hayer told DW, but he added that he had an ambivalent attitude to them. "On the one hand I can imagine that this will be a huge relief to many gamblers who had an addiction problem. On the other hand, if these people suddenly get a lot of money in their hands, but they haven't worked through their problems, then of course there's a danger of recidivism."
The legal obstacles
But Dünchheim suggested that the gamblers may not have such an easy ride when making their claims. It's true that German law has now concluded that if the gambling contract that the player makes with the company turns out to be unlawful in the country where they live, the player can claim their losses back. But only if the player themselves "did not act illegally," as Dünchheim put it.
"You also have to say: Many of these players deliberately went to games in this gray zone because the winnings are potentially bigger," he said. "Because the companies don't pay taxes."
"Then the defense team of the gambling company will of course say: 'You took part in an illegal game yourself, so you were acting illegally.' And this question of interpretation is not simple," he added. "It's a very interesting intellectual question, but it's also existential for the gambling companies."
Tipico's gambling gray zone
The Tipico case is perhaps particularly interesting in the German context because, although the company is based in Malta, it was founded in 2004 by a group of German lawyers. The company is a big employer, with several thousand employees worldwide, and has been a sponsor of more than one top German football club. Tipico has also said that it has rigorous consumer protection measures in place to identify and prevent dangerous betting behavior.
But there was some legal ambiguity about its online operations in Germany up until 2021.
"They always had lawyers who could attest that what they are doing conforms to European law, because it is permitted in a European Union member state," said Dünchheim. "But that is a false assumption, as it has now been established that a gambling permit in another EU state doesn't apply in Germany, because unlike other areas, gambling law isn't harmonized across the bloc."
"Tipico was started by two businessmen and grew big in a gray zone," as Dünchheim put it. "They had professional lobbying firms on board and they hired experienced lawyers, they had private equity firms on board. But of course they are carrying a huge financial risk."

description: German gamblers may finally be able to beat the house, thanks to new court rulings in the EU and in Germany. The decisions could help gambling addicts — but the legal road might be difficult.
content:
German gamblers could claim losses back
October 15, 2026
A German court has followed the European Court of Justice in finding that gamblers can seek compensation from gambling companies if they lost money when online casinos and fruit machines were illegal in Germany.
The verdicts could have major consequences for gambling addicts, as thousands of people could potentially bring civil lawsuits against gambling companies.
A series of court decisions at regional, federal, and European level have found in favor of gamblers in the last year, beginning with the Higher Regional Court Stuttgart in September 2025, which agreed with a plaintiff in the state of Baden-Württemberg who sued the Malta-based online betting company Tipico Games.
The plaintiff lost around €10,000 ($11,200) between 2020 and 2022, but because online gambling was prohibited in Germany until 2021, the court found that operators had therefore received the winnings without legal basis and must return them.
Wins for the losers
Tipico Games then appealed to the Federal Court of Justice (BGH), the highest civil and criminal court in Germany. In an initial verbal hearing in mid-September this year, the court followed the principle of the plaintiffs' case on one key point: That gamblers have the right to claim back losses if the companies did not have a license in Germany at the time the losses were incurred. But a final decision on the case is only expected to be made in January 2027.
Online casinos and fruit machines were banned in Germany from 2008 to 2021, but several gambling operators were active in the country because they had gaming licenses in other EU countries.
In April this year, the European Court of Justice ruled that EU law does not preclude a member state from "prohibiting certain services," or from "attaching civil-law consequences to that prohibition." In other words, even if a gambling company has a legitimate license in one member state, that doesn't override national gambling laws elsewhere.

title: Venezuela: Nicolás Maduro plädiert bei Folter-Vorwürfen auf nicht schuldig
content_c:
Venezuelas Ex-Staatschef vor US-Gericht Maduro widerspricht Folter-Vorwürfen
Venezuelas langjährige Staatschef Nicolás Maduro und seine Ehefrau Cilia Flores sehen sich in den USA neuerdings nicht nur dem Vorwurf des »Drogenterrorismus« ausgesetzt, zuletzt kam auch noch der Vorwurf der Verschwörung zur Folter hinzu. Diesen haben Maduro und seine Frau nun vor Gericht zurückgewiesen.
Maduro, 63, und seine Ehefrau, 70, plädierten vor Richter Alvin Hellerstein auf »nicht schuldig«. Es handele sich um »falsche Anschuldigungen«, sagte Maduro. »Ich weise dieses Dokument in seiner Gesamtheit zurück.« Der Richter unterbrach Maduro, als dieser weiterreden wollte.
Maduros Ehefrau Flores sagte: »Ich bin komplett unschuldig. Ich bin nicht schuldig.«
Maduro hatte sein Land an der Spitze einer sozialistischen Regierung von 2013 bis 2026 autoritär geführt. Im Januar waren er und seine Ehefrau in der venezolanischen Hauptstadt Caracas von US-Spezialkräften gefangen genommen worden. Seitdem sitzen sie in einem Gefängnis im New Yorker Stadtteil Brooklyn. Von Kritikern wurde das Maduros Gefangennahme durch die US-Kräfte als Verstoß gegen das Völkerrecht bezeichnet .
Die USA hatten Maduro und seine Ehefrau zunächst unter anderem wegen des Vorwurfs des »Drogenterrorismus« angeklagt. Auch diesen Vorwurf hatte das Ehepaar zurückgewiesen. Vor rund einer Woche kam dann zusätzlich noch der Vorwurf der Verschwörung zur Folter hinzu. Er bezieht sich auf die unrechtmäßige Inhaftierung und Folter von mehr als einem Dutzend US-Bürger in venezolanischen Gefängnissen während Maduros Amtszeit. Der Prozess gegen die Maduros soll am 1. Juni 2027 beginnen.
In Venezuela übernahm nach der Festnahme von Maduro die frühere Vizepräsidentin Delcy Rodríguez als geschäftsführende Präsidentin die Führung des Landes . In der Folge weiteten Caracas und Washington ihre Zusammenarbeit aus, insbesondere im Ölsektor. Die Wirtschaft des einst wohlhabenden Landes mit den größten nachgewiesenen Erdölvorkommen der Welt leidet unter Missmanagement, Korruption und Sanktionen.
Mit Perücke floh María Corina Machado aus ihrer Heimat, mit gebrochenem Rückenwirbel nahm sie den Nobelpreis entgegen. Venezuelas bekannteste Oppositionsführerin wartet auf die Rückkehr, die ihre eigenen Verbündeten hinauszögern. Das SPIEGEL-Gespräch lesen Sie hier.

title: EU-Methanverordnung unter Druck: Reiche fordert Aufschub
content_c:
EU-Methanverordnung Wenn Klimaschutz zur Verhandlungssache wird
Methan heizt das Klima deutlich stärker an als Kohlenstoffdioxid. Dennoch will Wirtschaftsministerin Reiche neue EU-Regeln aufschieben. Dokumente und Treffen mit der Gaslobby werfen Fragen auf.
Unsichtbar, aber klimapolitisch hoch relevant: Methan zählt zu den stärksten Treibhausgasen überhaupt und entweicht während des gesamten Wertschöpfungsprozesses fossiler Energieträger. Eine Tonne des Gases erwärmt das Klima innerhalb von 20 Jahren rund 80-mal stärker als die gleiche Menge Kohlendioxid. Daher ist die Verringerung von Methanemissionen eine der schnellsten Möglichkeiten, die Erderwärmung zu bremsen.
Genau dort setzt die EU-Methanverordnung an, die seit August 2024 in Kraft ist. Sie gilt als das weltweit erste umfassende Gesetz, welches die Emissionen langfristig erfassen und reduzieren soll.
Ein Gesetz gegen Methanemissionen
Ab dem 1. Januar 2027 sollten für Importeure von Öl, Gas und Kohle aus Drittstaaten neue Nachweispflichten gelten. Doch nun hat die EU-Kommission einen Vorschlag für einen einjährigen Aufschub vorgelegt. Sollte dieser beschlossen werden, müssten Importeure erst ab 2028 belegen, dass die Förderung der Energieträger nach Standards erfolgt, die mit den EU-Vorgaben zur Messung und Kontrolle von Methanemissionen vergleichbar sind.
Die Europäische Union ist bei fossilen Energieträgern in hohem Maß auf Importe angewiesen. Nach Angaben von Eurostat stammten 2024 rechnerisch 96,6 Prozent des verfügbaren Erdöls und der Mineralölprodukte sowie 85 Prozent des Erdgases aus Nettoimporten.
Bereits zuvor hatten mehrere EU-Staaten, darunter Frankreich, Italien, Tschechien und die Slowakei, eine Verschiebung der Vorgaben gefordert. Frankreich sprach sich für einen Aufschub um ein Jahr aus, Tschechien und Italien forderten drei Jahre.
Reiche stellt EU-Methanregeln infrage
Bundeswirtschaftsministerin Katherina Reiche (CDU) schloss sich den Forderungen nach einem Aufschub beim EU-Energieratstreffen im Juni an und stellte sich damit gegen den bisherigen Kurs der Bundesregierung, die Methanverordnung in ihrer 2024 beschlossenen Form umzusetzen. Bei dem Treffen des EU-Energierats sagte Reiche: "Wir müssen unsere Energieversorgung sichern, und wir befürchten, dass durch die Methanverordnung unsere Energiesicherheit gefährdet ist."
Während das Bundeswirtschaftsministerium die Auswirkungen der Verordnung auf die Energieversorgung betont, hält das Bundesumweltministerium an den bestehenden Vorgaben fest. Bundesumweltminister Carsten Schneider (SPD) sagte dem Handelsblatt: "Ich bin es leid, so zu tun, als gäbe es das gravierende Problem der Methanemissionen nicht."
Als Begründung für einen Aufschub verweisen mehrere EU-Staaten auf die angespannte Energieversorgung infolge des Iran-Kriegs sowie die Sorge vor weiter steigenden Preisen. Vertreter dieser Position argumentieren, strengere Vorgaben für Gas- und Ölimporte könnten Lieferanten abschrecken und die Energieversorgung zusätzlich verteuern. Ob ein Aufschub die Versorgung tatsächlich sichern würde, ist damit allerdings nicht belegt.
Treffen mit Lobbyisten
Kurz bevor sie sich öffentlich für eine Verschiebung der Vorgaben aussprach, reiste Reiche in die USA zu einem der größten Branchentreffen der Öl- und Gasindustrie. Auf der Konferenz erklärte Reiche, sie nehme bereits zum achten Mal an der Veranstaltung teil.
Recherchen von FragDenStaat zeigen, dass laut Vorbereitungsunterlagen innerhalb von zweieinhalb Tagen mehr als ein Dutzend Gespräche mit Vertretern von Energiekonzernen, Infrastrukturinvestoren und der US-Regierung vorgesehen waren, darunter mit BP und ExxonMobil über zusätzliche LNG-Lieferungen und die Umsetzung der EU-Methanverordnung sowie mit dem US-Innenminister Doug Burgum über Gaslieferungen.
Die vom Bundeswirtschaftsministerium herausgegebenen Unterlagen enthalten allerdings zahlreiche Schwärzungen. Betroffen sind Namen der Gesprächspartner, gleiches gilt für Teile der Vorbereitung zum Thema LNG und der EU-Methan Verordnung, auch Gesprächsnotizen und Protokolle fehlten.
"Gesprächsinhalte werden grundsätzlich nicht protokolliert", hieß es dazu auf Nachfrage aus dem Ministerium. Der Austausch mit Wirtschaftsvertretern gehöre zu den Aufgaben der Ministerin, so die Antwort aus dem Bundeswirtschaftsministerium weiter. Dies begründe "keinen Interessenskonflikt". Zur EU-Methanverordnung hieß es, dass die "Sach- und Rechtslage umfassend geprüft" werde. Die Bundesregierung informiere sich dazu "umfassend aus verschiedenen Quellen" und berate mit "Vertreterinnen und Vertretern der verschiedenen Interessengruppen". Eine Positionierung erfolge "nicht anhand eines Treffens".
"Rückendeckung des Bundeskanzlers"
Nach Recherchen vom Investigativlabel Cliff und FragDenStaat für den ARD-Podcast REICH - Das Geschäft mit dem Gas könnte die Konferenz in Houston nicht die einzige Gelegenheit gewesen sein, bei der Vertreter der Gasbranche ihre Position gegenüber der Bundesregierung vorgetragen haben. Am Abend vor einem richtungsweisenden Treffen des EU-Energierats im Juni kamen Wirtschaftsministerin Reiche und weitere Vertreter der Bundesregierung, von Bundesministerien, dem Bundeskanzleramt und Bundesbehörden in der US-Botschaft in Berlin mit Vertretern der amerikanischen Gaswirtschaft und der US-Regierung zusammen.
Zu den Teilnehmern gehörte auch Charlie Riedl vom Branchenverband Center for LNG, er äußerte sich bereits im Mai 2026 kritisch zur EU-Methanverordnung und erklärte: "Ich weiß, dass mehrere der Unternehmen, die der Verband vertritt, ihre Vertriebsmitarbeiter angewiesen haben, wegen der bestehenden Unsicherheit keine langfristigen Verträge abzuschließen." Wenige Stunden nach dem Treffen in der US-Botschaft sprach sich Reiche erstmals dafür aus, die Umsetzung der EU-Methanverordnung um drei Jahre zu verschieben.
Ein interner Ministeriumsvermerk, der Cliff und FragdenStaat von der Deutschen Umwelthilfe zugespielt wurde, legt nahe, dass die Ministerin dabei auf die "Rückendeckung des Bundeskanzlers" zählen konnte. Ob und in welchem Umfang die Gespräche mit Vertretern der Gaswirtschaft Einfluss auf die deutsche Position hatten, geht aus den vorliegenden Unterlagen jedoch nicht hervor. Was bleibt, sind die Fragen nach dem Einfluss von Interessenvertretern der Gaswirtschaft auf die deutsche Haltung zur Methanverordnung.
Am 29. Oktober tagt der EU-Energierat erneut. Sollte die Europäische Union die Importvorgaben der Methanverordnung abschwächen oder verschieben, könnte dies Signalwirkung für weitere Änderungen des Gesetzes haben. Das stünde dann im Widerspruch zum verbindlichen europäischen Ziel, bis 2050 klimaneutral zu werden, und könnte den Interessen der Öl- und Gasindustrie deutlich entgegenkommen.
Mehr zu diesem Thema hören Sie im ARD-Podcast REICH - Das Geschäft mit dem Gas.

Am 29. Oktober tagt der EU-Energierat erneut. Sollte die Europäische Union die Importvorgaben der Methanverordnung abschwächen oder verschieben, könnte dies Signalwirkung für weitere Änderungen des Gesetzes haben. Das stünde dann im Widerspruch zum verbindlichen europäischen Ziel, bis 2050 klimaneutral zu werden, und könnte den Interessen der Öl- und Gasindustrie deutlich entgegenkommen.
Mehr zu diesem Thema hören Sie im ARD-Podcast REICH - Das Geschäft mit dem Gas.

title: Хмельницький розривають вибухи — місто під атакою
content_c:
Хмельницький розривають вибухи — місто під атакою
У Хмельницькому зрання чути звуки вибухів.
Сьогодні, 16 жовтня, росіяни атакують ударними дронами Хмельницький.
Про це повідомляє кореспондентка ТСН.ua.
В області триває повітряна тривога — жовтий рівень.
Зазначимо, зо росіяни зрання атакують західні області України. Вибухи, зокрема, було чути в місті Рівне. Там, за даними місцевих ЗМІ, виникла пожежа.
Раніше повідомлялося, що в Умані внаслідок падіння БпЛА виникла пожежа в багатоповерхівці. Також поруйновано сторожовий будинок поруч: з-під завалів врятовано чоловіка.

title: Сможет ли Европа заменить США? Во Франции раскрыли объем разведданных, предоставленных Украине
content_c:
На фоне ограничения работы Starlink в Украине и передачи разведывательных данных из США министр иностранных дел Франции Жан-Ноэль Барро заявил, что страны ЕС предоставляют Украине две трети разведывательной информации.
"Напомню, что две трети разведывательных данных, предоставляемых Украине, сегодня поступают от европейцев, в частности от Франции", — сказал Барро в эфире France Inter, передает "Укринформ".
В то же время министр не смог опровергнуть или подтвердить информацию о том, что США сократили или прекратили передачу разведданных.
«В открытом доступе есть информация, которая, похоже, свидетельствует о снижении скорости работы Starlink», — отметил Барро.
На вопрос, способны ли Франция и Европа компенсировать возможные перебои в американской поддержке, Барро указал на совместные с Украиной усилия, в частности в сфере противовоздушной обороны.
«Мы работаем, в частности, над защитой украинского неба, над совместными проектами, чтобы как можно быстрее разработать ракеты для перехвата ракет, значительно дешевле и гораздо быстрее в производстве, чем раньше», — отметил он.
Ранее сообщалось, что у Европы нет быстрой замены Starlink и спутниковым данным США для Украины. Из-за проблем с этими сервисами затрудняются боевые миссии украинских дронов и раннее оповещение о российских ударах.

title: Буданов провів зустріч із міністром оборони Литви щодо спільних українсько-литовських проєктів
content_c:
Керівник офісу президента України Кирило Буданов у середу зустрівся із міністром оборони Литви Робертом Каунасом, темою обговорення стали російські удари по цивільній інфраструктурі та спільні проєкти, повідомив він у себе в Телеграм.
"Зустрівся з міністром оборони Литви Робертасом Каунасом. Обговорили поточну ситуацію на лінії фронту, зусилля України у напрямку дипломатії, суттєву ескалацію з боку рф та її підлі удари по цивільній інфраструктурі тилових міст України. Значну увагу приділили питанням реалізації спільних проєктів з виробництва зброї. Це критично важливо саме зараз, щоб зміцнити наші спроможності напередодні непростого зимового періоду. Маємо захистити життя та зірвати плани ворога. Дякую особисто пану міністру, Литві та всьому Литовському народові за тверду й безкомпромісну підтримку України. Працюємо далі", – йдеться у повідомленні.

title: Indian woman and boyfriend get death sentence in 'blue drum' murder case
content_c:
Indian woman and boyfriend get death sentence in 'blue drum' murder case
- Published
Warning: This story contains details that some readers may find distressing.
A woman and her boyfriend have been sentenced to death for the murder of her husband in the northern Indian state of Uttar Pradesh.
Muskan Rastogi, 26, and Sahil Shukla, 28, were convicted on 30 September by a court in Meerut city for the 2025 murder of her husband Saurabh Rajput.
Rajput's body was recovered from a large blue plastic storage container - locally called a drum - leading to the case being dubbed as "the blue drum murder".
Wednesday's death sentences have to be confirmed by the high court. Rastogi and Shukla have the option to challenge the verdict.
The prosecution said in court that Rastogi and Shukla had been classmates in school and had grown close in the absence of Rajput who worked in London.
When Rajput first came to know of their affair in 2021, he had wanted to get a divorce but was persuaded against this by his family since the couple had a young daughter.
Rajput was murdered on 3 March 2025 when he was visiting Meerut. Police said he was given food laced with sedatives by Rastogi before he was killed.
Rastogi and Shukla fled to Himachal Pradesh state but used Rajput's mobile phone to send text messages to his family to make it seem like he was alive and travelling for business, they added.
A few days later, however, Rajput's family lodged a complaint with the police saying that he was missing.
On 17 March, when Rastogi visited her parents after returning from Himachal Pradesh, her six-year-old daughter asked about her father.
Rastogi initially blamed her in-laws for her husband's murder. Unconvinced, her parental family took her to the police station.
Rastogi confessed to the crime during interrogation and she and Shukla were arrested and charged with the murder.
"My brother was killed by cruel people," Rajput's brother told BBC Hindi.
Rastogi's parents also demanded strict action against her.
"My daughter, along with a friend, murdered her husband in her own home. She is not fit for this society and is a danger to others," her father told ANI news agency.
Rastogi gave birth to a second child while in jail.

title: Number of cloned number plates on UK roads at record high, data shows
content_c:
The number of reported “cloned” vehicles involved in offences on UK roads has reached a record high, official data shows.
More than 11,400 drivers contacted the DVLA last year after being issued with fines for offences they said they did not recognise or accept responsibility for – most of which are believed to be down to cloning, where a number plate is copied fraudulently on similar vehicles to avoid enforcement cameras.
The number of complaints about misattribution was 9% higher than in 2024 and almost double the figure recorded in 2018, according to the RAC motoring organisation, which analysed data obtained under freedom of information requests.
The rising figures underscore concerns about the number of illegal number plates in use, allowing criminals to evade detection and dangerous drivers to avoid being caught.
Although drivers should provide number plate suppliers with the V5C vehicle logbook and proof of identity, an investigation last year uncovered more than 130 official suppliers in the UK willing to sell cloned versions, which allow drivers to dodge police and congestion charges.
Cloning vehicles has left many innocent car owners having to struggle to prove they were not responsible when enforcement camera images apparently caught their vehicle committing offences.
A parallel concern is the use of “ghost” plates which are designed to be unreadable by the UK’s 18,000 automatic number plate recognition (ANPR) cameras, which enforce safety measures such as speed limits or lane closures on smart motorways.
The RAC said the UK needed to overhaul an outdated and poorly regulated number plate system. Its head of policy, Simon Williams, said: “If number plate suppliers were carrying out all the checks they’re supposed to, it would be much harder for dodgy drivers to buy cloned plates in the first place. It’s only when a fine arrives at a vehicle keeper’s home address that they realise someone else is driving around using their vehicle’s number plate illegally.”
He said that more also needed to be done to catch drivers with ghost plates, “whether that’s more police officers being equipped with handheld devices that can detect if plates are unreadable, updating ANPR cameras and introducing higher security standards for number plates and for those who produce them”.
The government last month said there would be a new nationwide crackdown on illegal number plates, with funding from the Department for Transport for a new roads policing team. A new National Roads Policing Coordination Centre would share intelligence as well as trialling new technology such as specialised goggles to detect number plates that have been designed to be unreadable by cameras.
Drivers using an incorrectly displayed number plate can be fined up to £1,000.
A Department for Transport spokesperson said: “We’re cracking down on illegal number plates with significant investment in a new roads policing team and innovative tech to stamp out the scourge of cloned numberplates.
“Illegal number plates help facilitate crime, and we are supporting the police to work with the DVLA to make it easier to report these crimes and support victims through a new digital tool.”

title: School roof collapse in Pakistan's Peshawar kills dozens of students and one teacher
content_c:
Dozens killed in school roof collapse in Pakistan
Published October 15, 2026last updated October 15, 2026
Officials in Peshawar, Pakistan, confirmed on Thursday that at least 32 pupils under the age of 13 died when an elementary school roof collapsed in the Afridi Abad area of the city.
One teacher has also died, they said. The deceased, along with more than 50 other injured people, were brought to Lady Reading Hospital as rescue workers rushed to clear the rubble and search for more survivors.
"We have taken out at least 45 children," said district emergency officer Iftikhar Khan, but added that more children were thought to still be under the rubble.
From her hospital bed, a teacher told reporters that the school had three floors and more than 1,200 pupils and staff.
The cause of the disaster was not immediately clear.
Roof collapses becoming more regular
Local media in Pakistan noted that such incidents are becoming increasingly routine across the country, due to poor building standards and maintenance.
In July, three young girls were killed near Umerkot when the outer wall of a government school gave way. That same month, one child died and five were injured in Lahore when the roof of an under-construction private school collapsed.
One month earlier, 14 children were killed in a similar manner at a private tutoring facility in Lahore, which came shortly after yet another such incident in Dera Ghazi Khan.
Edited by: Natalie Muller
If you rely on our team for trusted reporting, please take a moment to select us as a preferred source on Google, so you'll always see our verified news first.

title: SPD: Doris Schröder-Köpf hört auf
content_c:
SPD verliert bekanntes Gesicht Doris Schröder-Köpf hört auf
Die niedersächsische Landtagsabgeordnete Doris Schröder-Köpf hat ihr Mandat niedergelegt. Die SPD-Politikerin verabschiede sich nach mehr als 13 Jahren aus dem Landtag, teilte die SPD-Fraktion in einem Post auf Instagram mit. Damit verliert die SPD ein bundesweit bekanntes Gesicht, auch wenn ihr Einfluss in der Partei als gering gilt.
Schröder-Köpf zog erstmals 2013 für die SPD in den niedersächsischen Landtag ein. Sie war jahrelang Landesbeauftragte für Migration und Teilhabe und leitete bis zuletzt den Ausschuss für Inneres und Sport. Die 63-Jährige war Schirmherrin der Stiftung Kinder-, Jugend- und Elterntelefone sowie der Drogentherapiestation des Kinderkrankenhauses auf der Bult in Hannover. Zudem setzte sie sich für Leseförderprojekte für Kinder ein.
Schröder-Köpf lebt mit ihrer Familie im Wahlkreis Hannover-Döhren. Sie war mit Ex-Bundeskanzler Gerhard Schröder verheiratet und später mit dem heutigen Verteidigungsminister Boris Pistorius (beide SPD) liiert.
description: Nach mehr als 13 Jahren im niedersächsischen Landtag hat die SPD die Abgeordnete Doris Schröder-Köpf verabschiedet. Die frühere Ehefrau von Ex-Kanzler Gerhard Schröder hatte sich vorwiegend im Bereich Migration und Teilhabe engagiert.

title: Brustkrebs: Mammografie-Screening künftig bereits ab 45 Jahren
content_c:
Vorsorgeuntersuchung Brustkrebs-Screening künftig bereits ab 45 Jahren
Bisher zahlen die Krankenkassen ein Mammografie-Screening zur Früherkennung von Brustkrebs bei Frauen erst ab einem Alter von 50 Jahren. Das soll sich nun ändern. Die geplante Neuregelung könnte im Sommer 2027 in Kraft treten.
Die spezielle Früherkennungsuntersuchung auf Brustkrebs, das sogenannte Mammografie-Screening, ist künftig bereits ab 45 Jahren möglich. Der Gemeinsame Bundesausschuss (GBA) beschloss, die Altersgrenze für die Teilnahme am Früherkennungsprogramm abzusenken.
Derzeit übernehmen die Krankenkassen die Kosten für diese spezielle Untersuchung der Brust mit Röntgenstrahlen im Alter von 50 bis 75 Jahren. Jüngere Frauen müssen die Kosten noch selbst tragen.
Der G-BA entscheidet, welche medizinischen Leistungen (Medikamente, Untersuchungen, Behandlungen) von der GKV gezahlt werden. Er ist also eine Art "oberstes Entscheidungsgremium" für die medizinische Versorgung von über 70 Millionen gesetzlich Versicherten in Deutschland.
Der Beschluss wird nun von der Rechtsaufsicht im Bundesgesundheitsministerium geprüft. Gibt es keine Beanstandung, tritt die Neuregelung zum 1. August 2027 in Kraft. Parallel aktualisiert der Bundesausschuss seine Versicherteninformationen.
Einladung zum Screening alle zwei Jahre
Frauen ab 50 Jahren erhalten aktuell alle zwei Jahre über eine Zentrale Stelle der Kassenärztlichen Vereinigung eine persönliche Einladung zum Mammografie-Screening. Die Untersuchung findet in spezialisierten medizinischen Zentren nach einheitlichen Qualitätsstandards statt.
Da sowohl die Zentralen Stellen als auch die medizinischen Zentren ihre Prozesse an die Neuregelung anpassen müssen, können sich Frauen ab 45 Jahren voraussichtlich ab dem Sommer 2027 direkt bei ihrer zuständigen Zentralen Stelle für einen Untersuchungstermin anmelden. Persönliche Einladungen erhalten sie dann vermutlich ab Januar 2028.
Sterblichkeitsrisiko bei Frauen gesenkt
Die Mammografie sei eine Röntgenuntersuchung der Brust und soll Tumore in frühem Stadium entdecken, bevor sie tastbar und Lymphknoten von Tumorzellen befallen sind. Laut einer Untersuchung des Bundesamts für Strahlenschutz, die sich über mehrere Jahre erstreckte, senkt das Screening das Sterblichkeitsrisiko für die Frauen, die teilnehmen, um 20 bis 30 Prozent.
Der Nutzen der Untersuchung sei zudem größer als die Strahlenbelastung, der die Frauen durch die Untersuchung ausgesetzt seien.
Mit Informationen von Daniela Remus, NDR

Через атаки РФ на енергоб’єкти, в Україні запроваджують графіки відключення світла 16 жовтня.
Раніше ми писали, чому в одних регіонах України є відключення світла, а в інших — немає.

title: Футболисты сборной Украины помогли "Бенфике" разгромить "Селтик" в Лиге Европы
content_c:
Украинские футболисты Анатолий Трубин и Георгий Судаков, забивший гол на прошлой неделе, сыграли за "Бенфику" в победном матче Лиги Европы.
Вратарь и полузащитник вышли на поле в стартовом составе на домашний поединок против "Селтика", который завершился победой португальцев со счетом 4:1.
Трубин в эпизоде с единственным пропущенным голом не лучшим образом сыграл на выходе, но при этом также совершил пять сейвов. Украинский вратарь в том числе трижды спасал свои ворота после ударов из пределов штрафной.
Портал Sofascore оценил выступление вратаря высокой оценкой 7,7 балла.
Судаков провел на поле 64 минуты на позиции плеймейкера без результативных действий. Тем не менее, хавбек успел создать пять моментов и отдал 35 передач. Украинский футболист исполнил пять угловых "Бенфики". Портал Sofascore оценил его игру в 6,7 балла.
"Бенфика" — "Селтик" — 4:1
Голы: Джон Дуран, 5 (с пенальти), 36, Ба, 23, Павлидис, 89 — Камило Дуран, 63
Видеообзор матча доступен по ссылке.
"Бенфика" одержала вторую победу в двух турах и входит в группу лидеров турнирной таблицы Лиги Европы.
Ранее сообщалось о том, что Мбаппе и Холанд побили рекорды Месси в Лиге чемпионов.

title: Внаслідок атаки РФ в частині Києва та Київщини відбулося масове знеструмлення – Укренерго
content_c:
У четвер НЕК "УКРЕНЕРГО" повідомила про масові відключення світла у Києві та Київській області внаслідок російської атаки на об'єкти критичної інфраструктурі, про це компанія повідомила у Телеграм.
"Внаслідок чергової російської атаки на об'єкт критичної енергетичної інфраструктури – в окремих районах Києва та області відбулось масштабне знеструмлення споживачів. Оцінка наслідків завданих ворогом пошкоджень та оперативні аварійно-відновлювальні роботи будуть розпочаті одразу після відбою повітряної тривоги, яка наразі триває на Київщині" – йдеться у повідомленні.
Також у компанії закликали споживачів у яких є електроенергія, зменшити її використання, задля запобігання відключенням та прискоренню відновлення живлення для інших користувачів.

title: They fled Russia, but the West sent them back
content_c:
They fled Russia, but the West sent them back
- Published
Russian security services were waiting when the flight landed in Moscow in December. On board were Russians the US had deported, including activists denied political asylum.
"It was unbelievably frightening. My knees were shaking with fear," says Katya, one of the deportees. We have changed her name to protect her identity, as she remains in Russia.
Katya had left Russia and claimed asylum in the US two years earlier.
When Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, many countries publicly welcomed fleeing Russians. But more than four years later, attitudes have hardened. The numbers of anti-war Russians forcibly returned from Western countries is rising, and Katya's experience highlights the potential risks they face.
US authorities rejected her application for asylum, after she said she had provided evidence that she had taken part in protests and was a member of an opposition movement.
In Moscow, Katya says officers from the FSB security service handed all the male deportees military papers, requiring them to register with the local enlistment office, from where men are often sent to the war in Ukraine. Another passenger on the flight and an activist confirmed her account.
The officers interrogated her, and many others, for several hours.
"At one point, they found incriminating information on my phone," says Katya, "Their faces changed in a second. I was very afraid that they would simply bundle me off somewhere."
Katya was eventually released and allowed to stay with relatives. But she says police continue to call her and visit her at home.
"I feel as if I'm in a cage, like in a zoo," she says, "Whenever I see a police car, I feel terrified and start thinking, "What if they're coming for me?"
Katya showed the BBC documents and photographs confirming her story, which matches accounts from other deportees.
Removals from the US rose from 222 in 2023 to more than 1,200 in 2025, amid a wider increase in deportations under President Donald Trump's second term. Activists say Russian deportees included dissidents and Russian army deserters, some of whom were imprisoned or sent to war after returning to Russia.
One such case is Leonid Melekhin, an anti-war activist who sought asylum in the US after being arrested at protests in Russia. He had posted photographs of Russian President Vladimir Putin online with the message "Putin: murderer, fascist, usurper". After being deported back home last year, Melekhin was charged with "justifying terrorism" and sentenced to six years in prison.
"We have several examples of people who got eight years in prison when they crossed the [Russian] border," says Andrei Pivovarov, from Russia's exiled opposition Anti-War Committee.
And deportations are taking place from Europe too. His organisation has changed its advice to dissidents escaping Russia: the EU is no longer safe, it is better to seek refuge elsewhere.
Germany has sharply increased the number of Russian nationals it deports. Seven were sent back in 2023, rising to more than 110 in 2025, according to German government figures. More than 21,000 Russians sought asylum in Germany between 2022 and 2025, but the proportion of positive decisions fell from 29% in 2023 to just 6.8% in the first eleven months of 2025.
"Protection is only granted if there is an actual, well-founded fear of persecution," Germany's migration and asylum agency, BAMF, told the BBC.
Last year, Berlin suspended its humanitarian visa programme for Russians, and across the EU, the proportion of Russian applicants granted some form of asylum protection fell from 23% in 2024 to around 17% in the first nine months of 2025, according to EU data.
Russian opposition activists fleeing repression have become caught up in a wider crackdown on immigration, as governments across Europe and the US toughen rules amid political pressure over high numbers of irregular migrants and asylum applications, as well as over security concerns.
Western governments are "focused on limiting humanitarian programmes and asylum seekers", says lawyer Anastasia Burakova, founder of rights group Kovcheg (Ark), which helps anti-war Russians leave the country. The clampdown is "in response to public concerns and rising support for right-wing populist parties", she adds.
Following a negative asylum decision, Russian nationals are often given the chance to leave independently, but a rising number are being forcibly returned to Russia, usually escorted via third countries.
Several Russian activists in exile told the BBC that immigration officials had told them they faced "no danger" in Russia, and that officials often lacked an adequate understanding of the risks that activists face.
"I tried to explain that if they sent me back, I would be put in prison, or sent to war where I'd be killed," explains former soldier Artyom, who deserted from the Russian Army in 2022 after officers threatened to send him to Ukraine. "They just didn't believe me."
He says he provided US authorities with proof that a criminal investigation had been opened against him back in Russia for desertion. But he was put on a deportation flight back to Moscow via Egypt.
"I was preparing for death," says the former soldier, "I was thinking, 'how can I die without it being painful?'".
Back in Moscow, Artyom was held in a military detention facility but managed to escape. He is now in hiding abroad.
"Another country could investigate me better and give me asylum. Why didn't they give me that chance? Instead they deported me specifically to Russia," says the deserter. "It ruined my life."
The US Department of Homeland Security told the BBC: "All illegal aliens receive due process. If a judge finds an illegal alien has no right to be in this country, we are going to remove them."
The asylum clampdown comes as repression inside Russia has reached "an unprecedented level", according to Nobel Prize-winning Russian human rights group Memorial. Their list of political prisoners grew from 803 to 1,265 during 2025, a record increase.
The Russian Embassy in London did not respond to a request for comment.
Anti-war activist Mikhail says he and his wife Dasha are awaiting deportation from Finland "any day". Their names have been changed to protect their identity, as Mikhail fears for relatives back home.
Russian authorities blocked his social media accounts over anti-war posts, and police visited his mother and accused him of spreading "fake information".
Dasha is a Jehovah's Witness, an organisation banned as "extremist" in Russia. The couple provided Finnish authorities with evidence, seen by the BBC, including a video of Russian police telling his mother that more than 300 posts had violated Russian law. A single post can result in a long prison sentence.
The Finnish Immigration Service has rejected their asylum request five times, deciding there is "no reasonable basis to believe" the couple would face serious rights violations if returned.
"We're sitting here and someone could knock on our door at any moment, take us to the Russian border and simply hand us over to Russian officers," says Mikhail. "We fear for our lives!"
"We came to Finland for help, and they're refusing us," he adds. "My wife cries constantly."
Amnesty International, which is supporting the couple, says they could face a "real risk" of detention, prosecution, imprisonment and torture if returned.
The Finnish Immigration Service said all asylum decisions were based on international refugee law standards, and the share of Russian citizens receiving asylum was in line with EU averages.
For Mikhail and Dasha, the threat of deportation comes as more Russians may be considering leaving.
There are rumours that Vladimir Putin may announce a new wave of mobilisation to boost the ranks of his army in Ukraine, which the Kremlin denies. The last mobilisation in 2022 prompted hundreds of thousands of Russians to flee, many to ex-Soviet states such as Armenia and Georgia.
Anastasia Burakova's organisation says requests for help from Russians wanting to leave rose tenfold in August compared with May. For those now looking to escape, the question is whether the West will offer them refuge — or send them back.

title: Farage accused of ‘protecting’ Reform candidate over racist slurs against David Lammy
content_c:
Nigel Farage was told by a senior Reform official that he was “protecting” a high-profile mayoral candidate accused of making racist comments about David Lammy, an undercover investigation has revealed.
The latest footage from an undercover investigation by ITV also shows Sarah Pochin, one of two female MPs for Reform, complaining that other party officials “are so fucking chauvinistic” and that “they just exclude you if you are a woman”.
Other footage shows Farage himself discussing the case of Chris Parry, a retired rear admiral picked to contest the Hampshire and the Solent mayoral election for the party.
The party stood by Parry for months after it emerged that he had said the former foreign secretary should “go home to the Caribbean” last year, and suggested that at least eight other politicians from minority ethnic backgrounds do not have a primary loyalty towards the UK.
However, while Reform eventually suspended him in March after the Guardian revealed other remarks by Parry, clips from an ITV documentary show Farage pushing back against senior advisers who said the candidate had to be sacked. They included Ed Sumner, Reform’s head of communications, who had told another press officer in an earlier disucussion that Parry was “clearly a racist”.
“He needs to go, I’m getting rid of him,” Sumner was filmed saying when the controversy broke last December. However, Parry was still the candidate three weeks later, while Farage told a press conference that the candidate could stay if he apologised.
In a conversation between Farage and Sumner, which was recorded by the undercover reporter, the Reform leader said that Parry “must apologise to Lammy” and was told that a text had been written for the candidate.
“He must do it and move on … Tell him that from me,” Farage said, to which Sumner said: “You’re protecting him.”
To laughter, Farage replied: “It’s showing a bit of … bit of sorrow. Look, ‘I’m sorry’ is probably a good thing to hear. Just take the fucking deal. Trouble is he’s a rear admiral. That’s the problem.”
Parry was suspended on 26 March after the Guardian reported that he had described members of a Jewish neighbourhood watch group as “cosplayers” and likened them to “Islamists on horseback”.
Bridget Phillipson, the Labour party chair, said these “latest shocking and deeply disturbing revelations go right to the top of Reform”, adding: “Nigel Farage needs to wake up and realise the buck stops with him. He also must urgently explain why he allegedly stood by a blatant racist instead of kicking him out of his party.”
The revelations are the latest in a number of recent controversies for Reform. The full ITV documentary, Undercover: A Year in Reform, airs on Sunday.
A number of councillors have already stood down after segments from the investigation aired on Wednesday showed them making graphic threats of extreme violence and expressing racist and misogynistic views.
The undercover reporter for ITV also met Pochin, Reform’s MP for Runcorn and Helsby, at a time when she was the party’s only female member of parliament.
When Pochin was told that a new female press officer was starting work, she was recorded as saying: “Oh thank fuck for that. God! We so need women press officers … They are so fucking chauvinistic.
“I go out on all the shows and go: ‘Oh no, it’s lovely, oh they’re all so welcoming.’ Shit … they just exclude you if you’re a woman. It’s really tough being a girl with all of this alpha male shit going on.”
Pochin did not provide a statement when approached by ITV. Reform UK used a statement issued on Thursday to accuse ITV and the company behind the documentary, Hardcash Productions, of using “extreme methods of deception”.
It said: “They have infiltrated our workplace including commissioning an undercover journalist to provide altered identification documents, a false address, and false credentials so that they could be given access to Reform’s headquarters, computer systems, and spy on its employees.
“That same journalist did not limit themselves to recording candid conversations in the workplace. That journalist also sought to find out sensitive security information, travel arrangements, and financial information outside of the scope of this investigation.”
Reform went on to claim that ITV had failed to address this in correspondence, despite this conduct being drawn to its attention. “This is at a time when Nigel Farage and other members of Reform are being targeted by individuals who wished them harm and caused a security issue which was documented during the course of the undercover investigation,” it added.
“There is no room for racism in Reform UK. We always respect due process of investigations and whilst these are ongoing it would not be appropriate to comment on individual cases.”
When approached for comment, Parry referred the Guardian to a statement given to ITV. In it he said: “I would urge people to go back to the original contexts and tweets to see what was said and why. They related to reparations and failures by the police and government. They will see I always exercise my right to criticise anyone in power or the public eye whom I judge to be acting against the interests of the British people.”

To laughter, Farage replied: “It’s showing a bit of … bit of sorrow. Look, ‘I’m sorry’ is probably a good thing to hear. Just take the fucking deal. Trouble is he’s a rear admiral. That’s the problem.”
Parry was suspended on 26 March after the Guardian reported that he had described members of a Jewish neighbourhood watch group as “cosplayers” and likened them to “Islamists on horseback”.
Bridget Phillipson, the Labour party chair, said these “latest shocking and deeply disturbing revelations go right to the top of Reform”, adding: “Nigel Farage needs to wake up and realise the buck stops with him. He also must urgently explain why he allegedly stood by a blatant racist instead of kicking him out of his party.”
The revelations are the latest in a number of recent controversies for Reform. The full ITV documentary, Undercover: A Year in Reform, airs on Sunday.
A number of councillors have already stood down after segments from the investigation aired on Wednesday showed them making graphic threats of extreme violence and expressing racist and misogynistic views.
The undercover reporter for ITV also met Pochin, Reform’s MP for Runcorn and Helsby, at a time when she was the party’s only female member of parliament.
When Pochin was told that a new female press officer was starting work, she was recorded as saying: “Oh thank fuck for that. God! We so need women press officers … They are so fucking chauvinistic.
“I go out on all the shows and go: ‘Oh no, it’s lovely, oh they’re all so welcoming.’ Shit … they just exclude you if you’re a woman. It’s really tough being a girl with all of this alpha male shit going on.”
Pochin did not provide a statement when approached by ITV. Reform UK used a statement issued on Thursday to accuse ITV and the company behind the documentary, Hardcash Productions, of using “extreme methods of deception”.
It said: “They have infiltrated our workplace including commissioning an undercover journalist to provide altered identification documents, a false address, and false credentials so that they could be given access to Reform’s headquarters, computer systems, and spy on its employees.
“That same journalist did not limit themselves to recording candid conversations in the workplace. That journalist also sought to find out sensitive security information, travel arrangements, and financial information outside of the scope of this investigation.”
Reform went on to claim that ITV had failed to address this in correspondence, despite this conduct being drawn to its attention. “This is at a time when Nigel Farage and other members of Reform are being targeted by individuals who wished them harm and caused a security issue which was documented during the course of the undercover investigation,” it added.
“There is no room for racism in Reform UK. We always respect due process of investigations and whilst these are ongoing it would not be appropriate to comment on individual cases.”
When approached for comment, Parry referred the Guardian to a statement given to ITV. In it he said: “I would urge people to go back to the original contexts and tweets to see what was said and why. They related to reparations and failures by the police and government. They will see I always exercise my right to criticise anyone in power or the public eye whom I judge to be acting against the interests of the British people.”

title: Germany news: Train station alcohol ban comes into force
content_c:
Germany news: Train station alcohol ban comes into force
Published October 15, 2026last updated October 16, 2026
What you need to know
These updates have been closed.
Below, you can read our roundup of headlines across Germany from Thursday, October 15.
- Train stations ban alcohol consumption nationwide after trial period in dozens of towns and cities
- Bundestag parliament approves reforms to emergency care services aiming to help paramedics and patients
- Sharp rise in tobacco taxes set for a vote in parliament, expected to pass
- Berlin left-leaning coalition negotiations likely to restart after major wobble earlier in the week
- Bleak potato harvest and higher prices forecast after scorching, dry summer
Tired of missing our real-time updates? Click hereto add DW as a Preferred Source on Google
German lawmakers turn their backs on AfD during genocide debate
Lawmakers from Germany's Left Party turned their backs on a far-right AfD politician after he questioned the historical consensus that Germany had committed genocide in what is now Namibia. The protest came during a heated debate over reparations for descendants of the victims.
Germany's government acknowledged the genocide in 2021, but parliament has yet to pass its own formal recognition resolution. A formal apology by Germany's president is also still pending. A proposed deal with Namibia includes €1.1 billion in development aid over 30 years, but no legally binding reparations. The agreement remains unsigned and controversial among descendants of the victims.
German carmakers eye looser 2035 EU emissions rules under revised deal
Germany and France reached a provisional agreement on Thursday that backs a scaling down of European emissions rules for new cars largely in line with the wishes of German carmakers, according to a draft document seen by news agencies.
The provisional agreement centers on a European Commission proposal last year backing off on banning new internal combustion engines by 2035, the new deal instead calls for a 90% drop in CO2 emissions from 2021 levels.
The remaining 10% was to be covered by compensatory measures like low-carbon steel and alternative fuels.
Now, the new agreement would scrap those measures, calling for the 10% to be compensated by manufacturers.
Europe's car industry, led by Germany, has been struggling in recent years amid the switch to electric vehicles and competition from China. This has led the EU to come up with ways to increase competitiveness while still maintaining pledges to reduce emissions. Germany and France have disagreed on how to do this.
The draft agreement still needs official confirmation. Then it faces approval by Germany's governing coalition led by the Christian Democrats (CDU), who have pushed for more watered-down emissions regulations than their Social Democratic Party (SPD) partners.
Then Germany and France will still need to convince other EU members and the European Parliament for the agreement to take effect.
Bundestag lifts immunity of SPD lawmaker, seemingly as part of corruption probe
The Bundestag has lifted immunity of a center-left Social Democrat (SPD) lawmaker, seemingly as part of a corruption probe pertaining to a tender for a hospital site in the northern city of Hanover.
Adis Ahmetovic, 33, had his immunity lifted so as to authorize searches requested by investigators.
He is one of three SPD politicians from the Hanover area under investigation in connection with the site in Lehrte, near Hanover.
The Hanover Public Prosecutor's Office said Ahmetovic's Bundestag office and three apartments were searched on Wednesday after his immunity was lifted.
The case came to fairly considerable prominence earlier in the year, because one of these politicians is Steffen Krach.
Krach was the lead SPD candidate for last month's state election in Berlin, and news of him being under investigation surfaced at the height of the campaign.
This may well have helped the Left Party and the Greens to fare better than predicted in the poll, while the SPD slumped to 12% — by far the party's worst ever result in the capital.
Alcohol ban comes into force at all German train stations
Alcohol bans came into force at all German train stations when the clock struck midnight and Thursday began.
All the roughly 5,700 stations across Germany, including the train platforms themselves, are now booze-free zones.
Pubs, restaurants and other such hospitality businesses at train stations are exceptions to the rule, though, and can still serve alcohol. Consumption of alcohol will also remain legal on many trains, with long distance ones still serving beers and other tipples at their on-board bistros.
Rail operator Deutsche Bahn says the change aims to make train stations safer and cleaner, and more pleasant places to spend time waiting for a (who knows, perhaps delayed) train.
Various misdemeanors and incidents had prompted discussions on alcohol at stations over the years, but two this year in particular brought the issues into sharp focus.
A 26-year-old security staff member for Deutsche Bahn was beaten and kicked by a drunken passenger when trying to check their ticket. During the struggle the train door buckled and opened, and the Bahn employee fell from the train, suffering severe injuries. Earlier in the year, a train conductor was killed when attacked by a man without a valid ticket.
The new rules are part of DB's house rules, rather than being criminal law — meaning that at least in the first instance it is a matter for Bahn security staff to enforce rather than police.
"The alcohol consumption ban applies at stations every day, also on days with major events," Bahn spokeswoman Anja Bröder said when asked about often beer-fueled train usage days, like when football fans flock to Bundesliga games.
Around 40 stations piloted the project for some time prior to its implementation, including some of the largest like Cologne, Munich, Hamburg and Berlin. DB says it has had positive experiences with the early experiments, reporting more peaceful stations with less litter and travelers and employees saying they preferred the atmosphere.
A federal group dedicated to helping the homeless has criticized the measure, however, saying that for homeless people with addiction illnesses, train stations often served as "important, weatherproof and comparatively safe places" to shelter. A spokeswoman also told the Rheinische Post newspaper that if they were driven from sites like train stations, it would be harder for social workers to locate them.
WDR's embattled 'Maus' mascot is given company outside Cologne HQ
German television's most famous orange mouse, WDR's eponymous star of the long running "Sendung mit der Maus" (Show with the mouse), stands in statue waving to whoever walks by the station's headquarters in Cologne.
And after a torrid few years for the celebrity rodent — in which he was kidnapped one year and set on fire by unknown assailants the next — now the mouse has been joined by its partners in crime the elephant and the duck, as was the case as the long-running show evolved.
"Life is always much better with friends," WDR Director General Katrin Vernau said at Thursday's unveiling. "Together the mouse, duck and elephant stand for a children's program that has conveyed knowledge for decades explaining the world and encouraging children to ask questions."
The children's show "Die Sendung mit der Maus" has been on WDR on Sunday mornings since 1971.
The show has various educational and entertainment elements and has had an array of presenters over the years, but the animated shorts featuring the mouse that separate the segments are probably the best known parts.
These short segments of perhaps 30 seconds of 2D animation never involve the mouse, or its accomplices the duck and the elephant who joined later, speaking.
Typically they interact and try to solve some kind of problem, often seeking a reward, by experimentation and trial and error.
Essen police continue search for prisoner and accomplices after violent escape
Police in Essen continued their search for a 34-year-old prisoner and the two men who violently freed him during a doctor's visit the previous day.
Officers searched parts of the city center, with the help of tracking dogs trying to catch the fugitives' scent.
Two men are thought to have attacked and tied up the prison officers accompanying the inmate on his medical visit, before the three of them split up and fled the scene. Police warned at the time that it "could not be ruled out" that they might be armed.
The 34-year-old was in the JVA Essen prison on drugs and assault convictions.
Bleak forecast for potato harvest and prices after scorching summer
Potato prospects this year are poor after the prolonged hot and dry weather in the summer, according to the government's statistics office Destatis.
"The 2026 potato harvest will be considerably more meager than the previous year, according to forecasts, which will have consequences for the prices of potatoes at various economic levels," Destatis wrote.
In September, Destatis said, potatoes were 11.3% more expensive than in the same month in the previous years. For frozen produce like chips/fries, the difference was less pronounced at 4.7%.
But these figures vastly outstripped both overall year-on-year inflation for September, 3.35%, and particularly the rate of inflation for food and drink products, 0.4%.
Destatis estimated that the 2026 harvest would be almost exactly one-quarter smaller than the previous year — partly because of fewer hectares being used to grow spuds but in larger part because of reduced average yields on the farmed soil in use.
Forecasts predict a yield of around 38.9 metric tons per hectare this year, compared to 46 tons per hectare in 2025.
READ: Hamburg court sentences Iranian agents for plot to attack Jewish leaders
A court in Hamburg has sentenced two men convicted of planning attacks in Germany on behalf of Iran's secret service.
One was given an eight-and-a-half-year prison sentence, while the other was ordered to spend four-and-a-half years behind bars on charges of espionage and attempted murder.
Among others, they were accused of plotting to attack Josef Schuster, the president of the Central Council of Jews in Germany and Volker Beck, a Green party politician and president of the German-Israeli society. Beck hailed the verdict online.
Bavaria's Ansbach named 2026 train station of the year
Choo-choo! All aboard the October 15 German rail news express, stopping wherever and whenever the conductor asks politely.
Ansbach train station in northwestern Bavaria, west of Nuremberg, has been named the finest in all the land.
The "Pro Rail Alliance" travel organization's special jury named Ansbach the Bahnhof des Jahres 2026, saying that after a renovation process lasting several years, it now "receives travelers in a light and friendly atmosphere."
They praised its well-lit waiting area, easy accessibilty by car, bike or bus, and ample storage for bicycles. They also noted its practical connection to the wider public transport network.
"Ansbach's bus station can be found right outside the train station building, and so can be reached with the greatest possible ease," the jury wrote.
If you're looking for a reason — other than the now alcohol-free train station, that is — to visit the town of roughly 40,000 people, you'll find it on the historic Castle Road from Heidelberg to Bayreuth. It's near the Frankenhöhe National Park, is home to the Ansbach Residence medieval castle complex, the picturesque Ansbach Court Gardens, an 18th century synagogue, and is also the site of the crypts of the Margrave noble family of Franconia.
Reforms to emergency service response pass Bundestag
The government's planned changes to emergency service response have cleared the lower house of parliament, the Bundestag.
One opposition party, the Greens, also supported the grand coalition's proposals, which are similar to plans that were under discussion in the previous government before it was cut short by early elections in 2025.
Health Minister Carsten Linnemann says the changes aim to ensure that patients receive care quicker, and in the right place.
Its main goal is to help ease the burden for paramedics and emergency first responders, by trying to prevent unncecessary calls to the 112 emergency hotline when a different service might be more appropriate.
Perhaps the main pillar of the plan is to directly network the emergency ambulance phone line 112, with the out-of-hours emergency doctor helpline 116 117 that is designed for less life-or-death medical cases.
Linnemann said the reforms were long overdue and that the reality was still that too many people did not really know who they were supposed to call when, and if in doubt would just call 112.
The reform package also envisages setting up integrated emergency centers, known by the German acronym INZ, that will be open around the clock and will bring doctors and hospital staff and other emergency responders together at one site.
Special emergency centers for children and adolescents will also be set up.
Welcome to our updates
Alla hopp! Another day, another digest of the main news morsels on the menu in fair Deutschland, delectable and perhaps disgusting alike. Thanks for stopping by, Planet Earth.
If you're waiting for a train and frustrated by the delay — hardly an unthinkable scenario in modern Germany — on no account crack open a beer to wile away the time. Starting this Thursday, booze is banned at all of the country's train stations. It's part of a bid to improve behavior, fight littering and in extreme cases protect travelers and staff alike.
Various reform plans should start the parliamentary reading process in the Bundestag, after the Cabinet signed off on them in a Wednesday meeting. These include hikes to tobacco taxes, emergency service reforms, and changes to the federal law on support in education.
The Bundestag will also vote, in what's probably a formality, on extending the military peacekeeping deployments in the Red Sea and in South Sudan into 2027.
Left-leaning coalition negotiations are set to restart in Berlin after hitting a big bump in the road earlier this week.
Essen police are still searching for a prisoner who was violently freed from custody yesterday by two accomplices during a doctor's visit.
And the government stats office is warning of a meager potato harvest and increased prices after the scorching, dry summer.
We'll endeavor to keep you abreast of these stories and whatever else breaks as the day develops.
description: Consuming alcohol is no longer permitted at train stations in Germany, to improve the lot of travelers and staff alike. Coalition talks are restarting in Berlin, and an inmate is loose in Essen.

title: Jemen: Bundeswehr-Einsätze gegen Huthi-Miliz verlängert
content_c:
Schutz von Handelsschiffen Bundestag verlängert Bundeswehreinsatz gegen Huthi-Miliz
Der Bundestag hat zwei Auslandseinsätze der Bundeswehr verlängert: Im Roten Meer sowie im Südsudan werden weiterhin deutsche Soldatinnen und Soldaten im Einsatz sein.
Die deutsche Marine beteiligt sich demnach weiterhin mit maximal 350 Soldatinnen und Soldaten an der EU-Mission »Aspides« im Roten Meer. Diese soll Handelsschiffe vor der aus dem Jemen agierenden und mit Iran verbündeten Huthi-Miliz schützen.
Bundesaußenminister Johann Wadephul (CDU) hatte für eine Fortsetzung des Einsatzes geworben. Die Angriffe der Huthi-Miliz auf zivile Handelsschiffe im Roten Meer gefährdeten globale Handelswege mit großer Bedeutung für Europa und Deutschland, sagte Wadephul. »Das zeigt, wie wichtig die militärische Präsenz der Europäischen Union in diesem maritimen Raum ist.«
Das durch die Huthi-Angriffe betroffene Gebiet sei ein maritimer Raum von besonderer geostrategischer Bedeutung für die internationale Handelsschifffahrt, argumentiert die Regierung. »Die Handelsroute durch das Rote Meer ist die kürzeste Verbindung zwischen Asien und Europa mit einem Volumen von 15 Prozent des weltweiten maritimen Handels vor Beginn der Angriffe.« Die Folgen der Huthi-Angriffe seien Ausweichrouten und erhöhte Frachtzeiten. Die dadurch entstehenden Kosten würden durch Reedereien und Unternehmen letztlich an den Endverbraucher weitergegeben.
Bundeswehr im Südsudan im Einsatz
Auch das Mandat für den Blauhelm-Einsatz »UNMISS« im Südsudan verlängerte der Bundestag bis zum 31. Oktober 2027.
Der Südsudan ist seit seiner Unabhängigkeit 2011 von Machtkämpfen und Gewalt geprägt. Seit 2025 hat sich die Lage erneut deutlich verschärft. Die Blauhelm-Mission soll den Friedensprozess unterstützen und Zivilisten schützen. Die Bundeswehr soll unverändert bis zu 50 Soldatinnen und Soldaten stellen, etwa für Führungsaufgaben, und bei technischer Ausrüstung und Ausbildung truppenstellender Nationen helfen.
Seit mehr als drei Jahren wird in Südsudans Nachbarland Sudan gekämpft, gemordet und gehungert, es ist ein alles verzehrender Krieg. Mehr dazu lesen Sie hier.
description: Die mit Iran verbündete Huthi-Miliz greift Handelsschiffe im Roten Meer an. Die Bundeswehr soll sich nun weiter an der EU-Mission »Aspides« beteiligen. Auch zum Einsatz im Südsudan ist eine Entscheidung gefallen.

Schutz von Handelsschiffen Bundestag verlängert Bundeswehreinsatz gegen Huthi-Miliz
Der Bundestag hat zwei Auslandseinsätze der Bundeswehr verlängert: Im Roten Meer sowie im Südsudan werden weiterhin deutsche Soldatinnen und Soldaten im Einsatz sein.
Die deutsche Marine beteiligt sich demnach weiterhin mit maximal 350 Soldatinnen und Soldaten an der EU-Mission »Aspides« im Roten Meer. Diese soll Handelsschiffe vor der aus dem Jemen agierenden und mit Iran verbündeten Huthi-Miliz schützen.
Bundesaußenminister Johann Wadephul (CDU) hatte für eine Fortsetzung des Einsatzes geworben. Die Angriffe der Huthi-Miliz auf zivile Handelsschiffe im Roten Meer gefährdeten globale Handelswege mit großer Bedeutung für Europa und Deutschland, sagte Wadephul. »Das zeigt, wie wichtig die militärische Präsenz der Europäischen Union in diesem maritimen Raum ist.«
Das durch die Huthi-Angriffe betroffene Gebiet sei ein maritimer Raum von besonderer geostrategischer Bedeutung für die internationale Handelsschifffahrt, argumentiert die Regierung. »Die Handelsroute durch das Rote Meer ist die kürzeste Verbindung zwischen Asien und Europa mit einem Volumen von 15 Prozent des weltweiten maritimen Handels vor Beginn der Angriffe.« Die Folgen der Huthi-Angriffe seien Ausweichrouten und erhöhte Frachtzeiten. Die dadurch entstehenden Kosten würden durch Reedereien und Unternehmen letztlich an den Endverbraucher weitergegeben.
Bundeswehr im Südsudan im Einsatz
Auch das Mandat für den Blauhelm-Einsatz »UNMISS« im Südsudan verlängerte der Bundestag bis zum 31. Oktober 2027.
Der Südsudan ist seit seiner Unabhängigkeit 2011 von Machtkämpfen und Gewalt geprägt. Seit 2025 hat sich die Lage erneut deutlich verschärft. Die Blauhelm-Mission soll den Friedensprozess unterstützen und Zivilisten schützen. Die Bundeswehr soll unverändert bis zu 50 Soldatinnen und Soldaten stellen, etwa für Führungsaufgaben, und bei technischer Ausrüstung und Ausbildung truppenstellender Nationen helfen.
Seit mehr als drei Jahren wird in Südsudans Nachbarland Sudan gekämpft, gemordet und gehungert, es ist ein alles verzehrender Krieg. Mehr dazu lesen Sie hier.

title: Schwache Kartoffelernte lässt Preise steigen
content_c:
Schwache Ernte Weniger Kartoffeln, höhere Preise
Der extrem heiße Sommer und verringerte Anbauflächen haben Folgen für die Kartoffelernte in Deutschland. Diese dürfte 2026 so gering ausfallen wie seit Jahren nicht mehr. Das lässt die Preise steigen.
Die schlechte Kartoffelernte lässt in Deutschland die Preise steigen. Im September mussten die Verbraucher bereits 11,3 Prozent mehr bezahlen als im Vorjahresmonat, wie das Statistische Bundesamt mitteilte. Die Steigerung lag damit deutlich über der allgemeinen Inflation von 3,3 Prozent.
2025 hatte es mit 13,9 Millionen Tonnen noch eine herausragend gute Ernte gegeben. Im laufenden Jahr werden nach vorläufigen Ergebnissen nur 10,4 Millionen Tonnen Kartoffeln eingebracht, was einen Rückgang um rund ein Viertel bedeutet. Weniger Kartoffeln wurden zuletzt 2018 geerntet (8,9 Millionen Tonnen).
Wegen des knappen Angebots sind die Erzeugerpreise bereits deutlich gestiegen: Die Landwirte erhielten im August um 61,5 Prozent mehr Geld für ihr Produkt. So stark ist der Kartoffelpreis auf der Erzeugerebene seit drei Jahren nicht mehr gestiegen. Für sämtliche pflanzliche Produkte haben die Erzeugerpreise um 12,3 Prozent zugelegt.
Verringerte Anbaufläche und Dürre
Die Gründe für die geringe Ernte sind eine um 11,1 Prozent verringerte Anbaufläche und die Dürre, in deren Folge die Kartoffeln kleiner ausfielen. Statt 46 Tonnen pro Hektar wie im Vorjahr konnten die Landwirte im Schnitt aktuell nur 38,9 Tonnen ernten.
Dennoch werden in Deutschland deutlich mehr Kartoffeln erzeugt, als für den Bedarf im Land benötigt werden: Der Selbstversorgungsgrad lag nach vorläufigen Angaben der Bundesanstalt für Landwirtschaft und Ernährung (BLE) im Wirtschaftsjahr 2024/25 bei 145 Prozent. "Ein großer Teil der Kartoffeln und Kartoffelprodukte wird also nicht für den heimischen Markt erzeugt, sondern exportiert", teilte das Statistische Bundesamt mit.
Bei den verarbeiteten Kartoffelprodukten für die Tiefkühltruhe wie Pommes oder Kroketten ist der Preissprung noch nicht angekommen. Hier lagen die Preise zuletzt um 4,7 Prozent unter dem Vorjahresmonat.

title: РФ масовано атакувала Умань: зачепило багатоповерхівку, у місті спалахнули пожежі – є поранені
content_c:
РФ масовано атакувала Умань: зачепило багатоповерхівку, у місті спалахнули пожежі – є поранені
Усім постраждалим медики надали допомогу на місці.
В Умані внаслідок падіння БпЛА виникла пожежа в багатоповерхівці. Також поруйновано сторожовий будинок поруч: з-під завалів врятовано чоловіка.
Про це повідомив очільник ОВА Ігор Табурець.
«Станом на зараз відомо про п’ятьох потерпілих. Троє госпіталізовані, іншим медики надали допомогу на місці. На іншій локації зайнялись торговельні склади. Пожежу локалізували», — зазначив.
Усі служби працюють на місцях ударів.
Раніше повідомлялося, що у Луцьку, Рівному та Ковелі пролунали вибухи на тлі атаки ворожих ударних безпілотників. Моніторингові канали інформували про рух кількох ударних безпілотників у напрямку обласних центрів.
