title: Европа хочет создать собственный SpaceX: Брюссель готовит ускоренную процедуру одобрения
content_c:
Европейский Союз намеревается как можно скорее дать антимонопольное одобрение спутниковому проекту, который рассматривается как европейская альтернатива компании SpaceX Илона Маска. Этому предшествовали интенсивные переговоры с участниками проекта — Leonardo SpA, Airbus SE и Thales SA, сообщил Bloomberg источник, знакомый с ситуацией.
По словам собеседника агентства, пожелавшего остаться анонимным, в течение последнего года переговоры были сосредоточены на выявлении и устранении потенциальных проблем с конкуренцией ещё до официальной подачи заявки на одобрение проекта.
Компании пока не подали соответствующие документы, однако чиновники ЕС ожидают, что это произойдет в ближайшие недели, добавил источник.
Совместное предприятие, известное под названием Project Bromo, получило поддержку председателя Европейской комиссии Урсулы фон дер Ляйен. Она назвала его потенциальным европейским лидером отрасли, заслуживающим поддержки на самом высоком уровне.
В то же время её заместительница, еврокомиссар по вопросам конкуренции Тереза Рибера, предупредила, что проект не может рассчитывать на автоматическое одобрение со стороны антимонопольных органов.
Цель инициативы — создать компанию, которая поможет Европе уменьшить зависимость от американских поставщиков спутниковых услуг, в частности SpaceX Илона Маска.
Однако проект столкнулся с сопротивлением профсоюзов и поставщиков, которые выражают обеспокоенность возможными последствиями для рабочих мест и конкуренции.
Кроме того, Project Bromo станет одним из первых испытаний обновленного подхода ЕС к слиянию компаний. Новая политика предусматривает более благоприятные условия для создания крупных европейских корпораций, способных конкурировать с американскими и китайскими компаниями.
В случае крупных сделок, таких как Project Bromo, регулирующие органы обычно проводят подробные предварительные консультации ещё до официальной подачи документов. Это позволяет заранее выявить и устранить потенциальные препятствия для одобрения.
Ускоренная процедура на практике может означать, что сделку одобрят после так называемой первой фазы антимонопольной проверки, которая длится чуть больше месяца. Это возможно, если компании предложат меры по устранению конкурентных рисков, например продажу части активов.
Если же опасения относительно конкуренции останутся, регуляторы ЕС могут начать углубленное расследование, которое продлится несколько месяцев. Только после этого они примут решение: разрешить слияние или заблокировать его.
Европейская комиссия, являющаяся исполнительным органом ЕС, а также Airbus и Leonardo отказались от комментариев. Представитель Thales не предоставил оперативного ответа на запрос журналистов.
В прошлом месяце Урсула фон дер Ляйен назвала Project Bromo примером крупной европейской компании, которая нужна Европе для лидерства в будущей космической экономике.
Её слова вызвали критику со стороны некоторых депутатов Европарламента.
В интервью Bloomberg TV Тереза Рибера подчеркнула, что публичная поддержка проекта со стороны председателя Еврокомиссии не означает ослабления регуляторных требований.
«Это не означает, что мы не будем применять и не будем обеспечивать соблюдение собственных правил», — заявила еврокомиссар.
Владелец SpaceX Илон Маск уверял, что спутниковый интернет Starlink останется доступным для Вооруженных сил Украины, несмотря на его несогласие с политикой Киева. Однако в ночь на 14 октября работа терминалов Starlink была ограничена, из-за чего пропала связь с дронами и сорвались несколько важных миссий.

title: У Шепетівському районі Хмельницької області пожежа на території нафтобази – ОДА
content_c:
У четвер російські БпЛА атакували Хмельницьку область, внаслідок ворожої атаки виникла пожежа на території нафтобази у Шепетівському районі, до ліквідації наслідків атаки залучили усі сили, повідомив голова Хмельницької обласної державної адміністрації Сергій Тюрін.
"Сьогодні ворог неодноразово атакував Хмельниччину безпілотниками. Працювали сили ППО. Є збиття. Унаслідок атаки виникла пожежа на території нафтобази у Шепетівському районі. До ліквідації наслідків залучені всі необхідні служби…", – повідомив Тюрін у Телеграм.

title: Are student protests being manipulated ahead of France's presidential election?
content_c:
Are student protests being manipulated ahead of France's presidential election?
- Published
The French passion for protest is legendary in Europe.
Over the last few years, we have regularly witnessed farmers angry about costly regulations lobbing manure at local mayoral offices, while masked youths periodically hurl homemade grenades at riot police in disadvantaged city suburbs.
For over three weeks now, thousands of students have barricaded entry to high schools and taken their grievances to the streets.
This Saturday, hundreds of new demonstrations have been announced across France.
Students are expected to be joined by workers' unions and key figures from the so-called "yellow vest" movement.
France's prime minister, Sébastien Lecornu, suggested this week that student anger was being manipulated as politics heats up ahead of next year's presidential election.
The gilets jaunes (yellow vests) demonstrated against cost-of-living hikes for over a year from 2018 - becoming one of the longest-lived protest movements in French history.
Jérôme Rodrigues, a prominent gilets jaunes activist, has used Instagram to encourage people to join Saturday's demonstrations.
The protests should give a voice to those who "want to be able to live decently, no longer have to count every cent, and no longer have to choose between eating and driving", he said in a video.
"Anger has no political party. An empty fridge has no political party," he added.
So what is going on in the EU's second largest economy?
Social unrest, government borrowing costs at eye-watering highs, a deeply divided French parliament and an apparent revolving door of exasperated French prime ministers - six prime ministers over the last five years - all claiming to want to reduce their country's public debt.
Is France at breaking-point - and what does this all mean for the eurozone currency the French are such a huge part of?

But with so many French citizens already visibly unhappy with the status quo, imagine the reaction if taxes were to increase, or welfare and education budgets decrease, further.
France's national motto is liberté, égalité, fraternité (freedom, equality and fraternity), but that is certainly not the sense you get on seething streets and in viral social media posts.
I met 17-year-olds Maxime, Madeleine and Elodie this week, perched on big green dustbins that have been used to block the entrance to their high school as part of the weeks' long protest.
They told me things were bad enough here, in the 3rd district of Paris, with holes in classroom walls, swelling class sizes and a dearth of teaching staff, but the teenagers were more than aware, they said, that the situation was far worse in their capital city's disadvantaged suburbs.
"France likes to speak of égalité," they told me "but the reality is the poor here are prejudiced against, while the rich benefit."
None of them will be old enough to vote in the presidential election in France next spring but they questioned whether the changing face of politicians in power made all that much difference anyway.
The three young women told me large-scale protests seemed the only way to get heard by French authorities.

  - Published8 October
They are part of a defiant French tradition.
Cultural icon Victor Hugo, the 19th-Century author of French Revolution classic Les Misérables, also an activist for the French Republic, proclaimed: "Si vous n'êtes pas contents, manifestez, criez, hurlez, mais ne subissez pas."
("If you are not happy, protest, shout, scream but do not give up and give in.")
Amongst crowds of protesting students walking through Paris on Thursday, I came across a number of mums, with placards around their necks, reading: "Mums in solidarity."
Were they there to protest or to protect their kids, I asked? "Both!" was the emphatic response.
Gwen, 37, said she and other mothers were taking it in turns every morning to co-ordinate between students and police at their local school lock-in.
This came after mounting accusations of police brutality, denied by France's interior ministry, during protests earlier this month in which hundreds were injured and a 15-year-old boy in the town of Lens lost a hand.
France's interior minister has since suspended the use of stun grenades by police at high school demonstrations.
Gwen told me she did not mind that her son was missing weeks of school as a result of the lock-ins. "It's a far better education for him to wake up to his civic duty and to fight for what is just in society," she said.
At Thursday's demo I also came across 17-year-old Lola and her mother, Sandrine, sharing a placard that said revolution was the most beautiful expression of humanity.
"My mum took to the streets in '68," Lola said proudly. "Now it's my turn. No point in waiting for the presidential election in France. We want change now."
Student protests in Paris in May 1968 are the stuff of legend in France. Demands for better education inspired workers to join the marches which turned into the biggest general strike in French history. It set the standard for revolutionary upheaval for a generation and is credited with creating new opportunities for the French left.
Now, though, with six months to go before an already fraught presidential election in France, there are accusations that the hard left, under presidential hopeful Jean-Luc Mélenchon, is weaponising student frustration.
"Members of [Mélenchon's] France Insoumise (LFI) are instrumentalising the high school movement for their electoral advantage," said Sébastien Lecornu on Wednesday. He accused them of encouraging protests, then going through the motions of condemning any violence.
"This hypocrisy damages France," said Lecornu.
But "Mélenchon for President!" is a chant you often hear amongst the students in the streets.
Supporters applaud his desire for a wealth tax in France, for lowering the voting age to 16 and for being the only presidential candidate to turn up to French schools to examine the state of them, several demonstrators told me.
For Marine Le Pen, the nationalist anti-immigration favourite in France's presidential race, the solution is cutting the country's €11bn contribution to the EU's budget.
There is, though, reason to doubt that any new French president, from the left or the right, will be able to break the impasse over France's finances.
France is far from alone in Europe right now faced with an ageing population, a generous welfare state to run and a national economy squeezed by outside pressures such as US President Donald Trump's trade tariffs and the war in the Persian Gulf.
Whether in France, Germany, Sweden or Italy, there is an inherent tension between politicians who hesitate to tell voters the truth about shrinking public finances, the defence establishment's demand for higher defence spending and citizens' insistence on improved public services.
In France, that pressure is particularly acute. French public expenditure, at about 57% GDP, is one of the steepest amongst wealthy nations worldwide.
Social spending, particularly on pensions, is exceptionally large, while French citizens pay one of the highest overall tax and social contribution burdens in Europe. Simply put, they expect a welfare and public service bang for their buck.
But economist Anne-Laure Delatte does not believe having a new president will ease her country's financial migraine.
"We need constitutional change. A new system. A new Republic," she told me.
"Our Fifth Republic is centred around a powerful president. Parliament is there to block him or her rather than to find consensus or to make new laws."
For France to progress, she says, that has to change.
The French parliamentary election that follows the 2027 presidential vote is likely to be as divided as ever, she believes: "We need a system where MPs have more power and should learn consensus and coalition-building from our European neighbours."
In her opinion, education had to be protected and funds better distributed. It was an investment in France's financial future, she told me.
"Our current system of inequality in schooling and low wages for teachers means we lose out from benefiting from the best and brightest across French society. That is not only unfair on individuals but our economy ultimately loses out on innovation and productivity."
Re-writing France's constitution is not on the cards, at the moment. So, what about the here and now, I asked centrist politician Anne-Catherine Loisier.
She's a senator for the Centrist Union in France's upper house of parliament and vice president of the parliamentary group for sciences and technology.
Loisier, along with pretty much every leading French politician across the political spectrum, says the protesting students "must feel heard".
"Our budgets are limited," she admitted, "but you don't necessarily need more money. You can make improvements by redistributing funding better. Education is a regional competence in France. Every region should take a look at local needs and address priorities accordingly. That action can be taken immediately."
I asked Loisier if she agreed with UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham, the former mayor of Greater Manchester, that regions should be given greater powers. "Absolutely," she replied. "France has traditionally been very Paris-centric but so much could be improved by decentralising the country."
"My France isn't broken. I don't recognise that image you see portrayed in the media. My country is made up of lots of Frances. Paris, the regions; northern and southern France. We need to give power back to the people. Local governments can look people in the eye directly, so voters feel they have power over their own future, rather than politicians handing them their fate from up high in Paris."
"That way I hope we can restore voters' - and students' - faith in politics."
It's a promise you hear from politicians - right and left - ahead of France's huge elections next year.
But opinion polls here, as across most of Europe, indicate public faith in the political class is in dwindling supply.

title: Russell Brand made alleged rape victim take photos of him half naked, trial told
content_c:
Russell Brand transformed into a “monster” when he allegedly made a woman take half-naked photographs of him before raping her in a hotel room at a Labour party conference, a court has heard.
The 51-year-old comedian has denied attacking the woman, who broke down in tears in the witness box at Southwark crown court as she told how she could not fight him off.
“He was really heavy,” she said. “I couldn’t struggle. I couldn’t breathe. I know he raped me, I know I said: ‘No, no, I don’t want this.’”
Brand faces three charges of rape, three of sexual assault and one of indecent assault against six women, in allegations spanning 10 years from 1999 to 2009. He denies all the charges and has pleaded not guilty.
Brand fixed his gaze on one of the TV screens in court on Thursday morning as a video of the woman’s interview from 27 September 2023 was played. She told police she met Brand at a fringe cabaret event that he was performing in during the Labour party conference in Bournemouth in 1999. She was not attracted to the then unknown performer, whom she assumed was gay and who showered her with compliments.
But she found him polite and intelligent, and the pair spoke about their work before going back to her hotel room to continue their conversation.
The woman said she “froze” in the run-down single room when she returned from the toilet to find that Brand was partly naked and “prancing around” like an ostrich. She said she asked him why he had undressed, and he told her: “Don’t worry, I’m mostly naked at home.”
The woman told how she became “frightened” when Brand made her take half-naked photographs of him. “I took pictures of him on my camera – he made me take them,” she said. “I remember feeling: ‘What on earth have I got myself into?’”
She told police he then raped her in an attack that lasted up to 10 minutes and left her feeling scared, in pain, and as if she couldn’t breathe.
“He did rape, he did push me on the bed,” she told police. “He did pull my clothes off, he took my trousers off.
“I remember him on me, very heavy. I know I said no. I kind of drifted out of my head. I couldn’t get out of the situation – ‘do I shout, do I scream?’ He was very heavy, I couldn’t breathe, it didn’t take long.”
She described his body as snake-like and “disgusting” and said his tongue was “horrible” like a lizard. “I’m saying ‘no, no’ but I was really scared,” she told police. “I know he groped me. I know he was touching me, I know he grabbed my breasts. I know he tried to kiss me and I moved my neck. I didn’t want his mouth on mine.
“He was just pulling my trousers down and pulling my underwear off, and he was inside me. It was not nice, it was painful and it hurt.”
Giving evidence from behind a screen in the afternoon, the woman added: “I was like a zombie on the bed. All I could think was he’s inside me and the quicker the better.”
In tense exchanges during cross-examination with the defence barrister, Ian Winter KC, the woman denied that Brand had persuaded her to have sex. “He was frightening, he seemed menacing at that point,” she replied. “He’s scary. I didn’t know what to do.”
She rejected Winter’s suggestion that she had fallen under the spell of Brand, whom the barrister described as charismatic with a magnetic personality. The judge, Mr Justice Bennathan, had to interrupt the lawyer during one exchange to object to one of his questions, saying: “Shush please. I’m the judge, you have to let me talk.”
The woman told the court Brand was a “completely different persona” in the hotel room. When pressed further by the prosecutor, Riel Karmy-Jones, the woman said: “He just changed suddenly from camp, friendly and effeminate to monster-like.
“I felt very scared in that moment. He was big, I felt threatened and he’s half naked. And while I’m naive, I didn’t think at that moment his intentions were good.
“He was just dark and arrogant and performing – he was scary, he was demanding. He was the centre of the show, it was like it was back on stage – he wasn’t the [same] person I was chatting to.”
The woman told police she closed her eyes during the attack and that Brand made her feel sick and dirty. She recalled: “He was making noises, a lot of noises of enjoyment and saying how pretty I was. I remember him complimenting me, saying: ‘Are you enjoying it’? I remember him asking me. Obviously I didn’t answer.”
She alleged that Brand spoke as the attack was unfolding. She told police: “He was just saying: ‘We’re having fun, it’s fine, it’s all good, don’t worry about it, it’s just fun, it’s normal.’”
The woman, who had been a victim of abuse in the past, said Brand made her compare earlier experiences, and it “stuck in her head … is this what abusers do?”
She told police: “It was almost like to convince me it’s all OK and that I’d enjoy it, that I’d have to learn to enjoy it.”
In the aftermath, she said Brand acted “like nothing was wrong”, wrote down his email address, and suggested that his mother might like to meet her.
She told the court: “He is so arrogant in his mindset that he’s God’s gift that I must’ve enjoyed it and I must’ve wanted more.”
The following morning, she banged her head against the wall because she felt numb. She told police she had had nightmares about being pregnant and said she kept quiet about the incident for years as she watched Brand becoming “more and more famous”.
The woman said a 2023 Dispatches documentary about allegations of sexual misconduct by Brand “triggered” her to go to police.
Brand denies the allegations. The trial continues.

title: Brazil's elections matter for the planet. This is why
content_c:
Why Brazil's elections matter for the planet
October 15, 2026
Few national elections carry as much environmental weight as Brazil's presidential race. And this one is being watched from far beyond the country's boundaries.
Home to the largest section of the Amazon rainforest, Brazil is guardian of a carbon sink of vital importance, making the country's conservation policies globally relevant.
Environmentalists have already voiced alarm at Flávio Bolsonaro — son of right-wing former president Jair Bolsonaro — coming out 2% ahead of incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in the first round of elections.
"It's going to be a second coming of Bolsonaro, therefore a more radical Bolsonaro," said Claudio Angelo, international policy coordinator at Climate Observatory, a network of Brazilian NGOs.
"At the risk of sounding alarmist, I would say Lula's re-election is the only thing standing between us and the end of the Amazon."
Amazon rainforest: One of nature's most powerful defenses
The Amazon rainforest stores huge amounts of the carbon dioxide (CO2) released into the atmosphere from the burning of fossil fuels. As a result, it helps regulate the Earth's climate.
For decades, the tropical forest has acted as one of nature's most powerful defenses against climate change. But it has also suffered from widespread deforestation.
During Jair Bolsonaro's presidency, from 2019 until 2023, environmental agencies were weakened and enforcement efforts curtailed, meaning tropical forest was cleared at unprecedented rates.
"The environment agenda was disregarded and the level of control the government had on pollution overall, but specifically on deforestation, was reversed," said Claudio Forner, head of climate policy at Berlin-based think tank Climate Analytics.
Over Bolsonaro's four-year term, an estimated 45,586km2 of the Amazon was destroyed, an area bigger than the size of Denmark. And the forest is not as resilient as it once was, with scientists warning that parts of it are now emitting more carbon than they absorb.
Lula came to office with a message of protection for the Amazon. Besides calling for an end to deforestation by 2030, he increased monitoring of the forest and strengthened Brazil's environmental enforcement agency IBAMA.
Deforestation has plummeted under his leadership, with 2026 set to be its lowest level in a decade. That represents a 41% drop overall compared to Jair Bolsonaro's tenure.
Pitting environment against the economy
Experts have already criticized Flávio Bolsonaro's record on forest protection. As a senator in 2019, he authored draft legislation that could have stark impacts for the Amazon. While landowners are currently required to preserve 80% of their property for the growth of native plants, the bill would allow them to use their holdings as they please.
"The signal from the president will say 'now you can deforest' or 'it's harder to deforest,'" said Ana Yang, director of the Environment and Society Center at London-based think tank Chatham House.
"The moment that you decrease enforcement capability, deforestation grows," she told DW.
Bolsonaro has also pledged to end illegal deforestation by 2029, a year before Lula. But Claudio Angelo is critical of that message.
"He will end illegal deforestation not by enforcing the law, but by making it legal," he said.
More generally, environmental experts fear Bolsonaro might dismantle many of the protections strengthened under the current president.
"Unfortunately, climate change has become a partisan issue, so rather than offering a solution from their perspective, the right pictures climate change as an invented problem...that regulation goes against economic growth or it goes against competitiveness, that it's the aim of the left to control the means of production," Forner said.
In an interview with Brazilian media in August, Bolsonaro said he regarded extreme weather events to be cyclical and did not believe they were solely linked to human influence.
No straightforward climate success story for Brazil
A Bolsonaro win is likely to see Brazil move away from its position as a climate leader, a role the country embraced last year as it hosted the COP30 climate conference in the Amazonian city of Belem.
But even a Lula victory would not represent a straightforward climate success story, say experts. While the current administration has overseen significant reductions in deforestation, it has also backed plans to expand oil production.
Angelo said the decision to allow exploratory drilling was a "betrayal" of Lula's mandate but added that the president's overall record on climate had been "quite impressive".
"Lula is the world's worst climate leader, except for all the others," he told DW.
The current president will face a runoff election with Bolsonaro on October 25. But while experts say the outcome could determine the fate of the Amazon and the wider efforts to curb global warming, for many Brazilians climate is not high on their list of priorities.
"Ultimately what people care about is access to education, sanitation and health," said Yang. A road built through the Amazon to access those services, while criticized from outside Brazil for destroying parts of the rainforest, would be desirable to voters, she added.
"They don't have time to care. Not because they don't want to. They care about their own survival," she said.
Edited by: Tamsin Walker

title: EZB erlaubt UniCredit offenbar Übernahme von Commerzbank
content_c:
Bankenkampf EZB erlaubt UniCredit offenbar Übernahme von Commerzbank
Die UniCredit bekommt nach eigenen Angaben grünes Licht von der EZB-Bankenaufsicht für die Übernahme der Commerzbank. Damit kann die italienische Großbank die Commerzbank-Aktien, die sie sich im Sommer über ein Tauschangebot gesichert hatte, in eigene Anteile umwandeln.
Die Europäische Zentralbank habe die Übernahme der Kontrolle über die Commerzbank genehmigt, teilte UniCredit mit. Man habe die Genehmigung erhalten, die Schwelle von 30 Prozent der Kapitalbeteiligung an der Commerzbank zu überschreiten und den Anteil ohne Obergrenze weiter zu erhöhen.
»Die Entscheidung stellt einen wichtigen Meilenstein bei der Übernahme der Commerzbank durch UniCredit dar und unterstreicht die positive Bewertung der Transaktion durch die EZB sowie das Vertrauen in die soliden Fundamentaldaten und die starke Position von UniCredit innerhalb des europäischen Bankensektors«, hieß es weiter.
Die verbleibenden aufsichtsrechtlichen Verfahren und Bedingungen für den Abschluss des Angebots für die Commerzbank würden demnach voraussichtlich gegen Jahresende abgeschlossen sein. Zu diesem Zeitpunkt werde UniCredit über rund 50 Prozent der Stimmrechte an der Commerzbank verfügen und die Kontrolle über die Bank übernehmen können, hieß es.
Angebot im Mai vorgelegt
Die Großbank aus Mailand hatte im Mai ein Angebot für sämtliche Commerzbank-Aktien vorgelegt und sich so Zugriff auf knapp die Hälfte der Anteile an dem Dax-Konzern gesichert – teils auch indirekt über komplexe Finanzgeschäfte. Für einen Vollzug des Aktientauschs stand aber noch die EZB-Genehmigung aus, die als zentraler Schritt gilt. Nun steigt der Aktienanteil der UniCredit an der Commerzbank von knapp 30 auf fast 50 Prozent.
Die Bankenaufsicht der Europäischen Zentralbank (EZB) überwacht die größten Geldhäuser im Euroraum. Ihre Erlaubnis kommt nicht überraschend: Sie hat immer wieder deutlich gemacht, dass sie grenzüberschreitende Bankenfusionen im Euroraum befürwortet, um den EU-Binnenmarkt zu stärken.
Die UniCredit kann nun weitere Commerzbank-Aktien frei am Markt kaufen. Die Italiener könnten auch ein weiteres Angebot vorlegen, was aber wegen der üblichen Übernahmeprämie teuer wäre.
Bund will betriebsbedingte Kündigungen vermeiden
Die UniCredit bemüht sich seit rund zwei Jahren um die Commerzbank und hat ihren Anteil trotz des Widerstands aus Deutschland immer weiter ausgebaut. Die Mailänder Großbank, die in Deutschland bereits mit der HypoVereinsbank (HVB) vertreten ist, sieht Potenzial für Milliardeneinsparungen inklusive des Abbaus Tausender Stellen. Inzwischen führen UniCredit und Commerzbank Gespräche über einen möglichen Zusammenschluss.
Der Bund, der mit seinem Commerzbank-Anteil von gut 13 Prozent ein Wort mitzureden hat, will betriebsbedingte Kündigungen bei dem Dax-Konzern mit seinen weltweit rund 40.000 Vollzeitkräften möglichst verhindern. Er will erreichen, dass die Commerzbank eine börsennotierte Aktiengesellschaft mit Sitz in Frankfurt bleibt und ihr starkes Mittelstandsgeschäft fortsetzt.

title: SPD wählt Mitte Januar bei Parteitag in Bremen neue Parteispitze
content_c:
Bundesparteitag in Bremen SPD wählt Mitte Januar neue Parteispitze
Seit dem Rückzug von Bärbel Bas fehlt der SPD die Hälfte ihrer Doppelspitze. Nun will die Partei ihre gesamte Führung neu wählen. Bewerbungen liegen noch nicht vor, aber es gibt Zeit und Ort für den Bundesparteitag.
Nach dem Rücktritt von Bärbel Bas läuft in der SPD die Debatte über eine Neubesetzung des Parteivorsitzes. Mehrere Namen kursieren, offizielle Bewerbungen gab es aber noch nicht. Was es aber inzwischen gibt: einen Termin für den Parteitag. Wie das ARD-Hauptstadtstudio aus Parteikreisen erfuhr, soll der SPD-Bundesparteitag am 16. und 17. Januar in Bremen stattfinden. Dort werde der gesamte Parteivorstand neu gewählt.
Tritt Klingbeil wieder an?
Nach Bas' Rücktritt am Montag hatte sich das SPD-Präsidium auf Vorschlag von Parteichef Lars Klingbeil einstimmig für eine Neuwahl der gesamten Spitze ausgesprochen. Klingbeil selbst hält offen, ob er noch mal antritt.
Der Vizekanzler und Finanzminister ist in der Partei längst nicht mehr unangefochten. Auf dem vergangenen Parteitag war er nur mit einem enttäuschenden Ergebnis von 64,9 Prozent wiedergewählt worden, während Bas mit 95 Prozent ein sehr gutes Ergebnis erhielt. Die Unzufriedenen mit dem Regierungskurs machen eher Klingbeil als Bas für Kompromisse in der schwarz-roten Koalition verantwortlich. "Ich weiß doch, welche Kritik es auch gibt", sagte Klingbeil kürzlich im ZDF. Er klebe nicht an seinem Amt, bekräftigte er in ARD-Interviews.
Kein Gedrängel um das Führungsamt
Klingbeil möchte am Prinzip Doppelspitze festhalten. Kandidatinnen für den Spitzenplatz neben Klingbeil drängeln sich bislang nicht nach vorn. Im Gegenteil: Saarlands Ministerpräsidentin Anke Rehlinger sagte definitiv ab, schon weil sie sich 2027 einer Landtagswahl stellen muss. Manuela Schwesig hat die Wahl gerade einigermaßen erfolgreich hinter sich gebracht - und strickt nun an einer Dreierkoalition. Sie gilt als wortgewandt und angriffslustig, es zieht sie aber nach eigenen Angaben auch nicht an die SPD-Spitze.
Schwerin oder Berlin - wohin geht Manuela Schwesig?
Ämtertrennung und Neustart?
Sowohl Klingbeil als auch Bas waren beziehungsweise sind zugleich Parteivorsitzende und Bundesminister. Im Zuge der geplanten Neuwahl der SPD-Spitze läuft auch wieder eine Diskussion über die Trennung dieser Ämter.
Juso-Chef Philipp Türmer sieht den Parteitag als Möglichkeit für einen Neustart der SPD. In einer am Freitag erscheinenden Ausgabe des ARD-Mediatheks-Formats Draußenpolitik sagt Türmer, er habe nicht den Eindruck, dass die Doppelrolle aus Kabinett und Parteivorsitz in der letzten Zeit funktioniert habe. "Ich könnte mir gut vorstellen, dass wir auch eine Einzelspitze haben. Wenn wir jetzt zum Beispiel sagen würden, es macht eine Frau allein. Das fände ich ziemlich cool. Das könnte ich mir sehr gut vorstellen", so Türmer.
Bis Mitte Januar gibt es für die SPD also noch viel zu diskutieren - über Personal und Inhalte.

title: Через одну помилку в трудовій книжці можна втратити пенсію: що необхідно перевірити
content_c:
Через одну помилку в трудовій книжці можна втратити пенсію: що необхідно перевірити
Навіть дрібні помилки в датах або відсутність однієї печатки в трудовій книжці можуть заблокувати зарахування страхового стажу під час оформлення пенсійних виплат.
При оформленні пенсійних виплат навіть незначні помилки в трудовій книжці часто призводять до додаткових перевірок. Пропущені печатки, відсутність підписів чи помилки в датах суттєво ускладнюють підтвердження страхового стажу.
Необхідно завчасно переглянути свої документи, щоб без поспіху виправити помилки й у разі потреби зібрати необхідні довідки, повідомляє видання «На пенсії».
Що обов’язково треба перевірити в трудовій книжці перед оформленням пенсії
Перш за все варто перевірити першу сторінку трудової книжки, де зазначені особисті дані власника. Важливо переконатися, що прізвище, ім’я та по батькові вказані правильно, а дата народження відповідає даним паспорта або іншого документа, що посвідчує особу.
Також потрібно звернути увагу на оформлення першої сторінки. Відповідно до норм, які діяли під час її заповнення, там обов’язково мають стояти підписи власника та відповідального працівника, а також печатка організації чи кадрового відділу.
Також необхідно ретельно звірити записи про прийняття на роботу та звільнення. Переконайтеся у відсутності помилок у датах, назвах компаній і посадах, а також у тому, що формулювання про звільнення засвідчені належним чином згідно з тогочасними правилами.
При цьому слід враховувати, що стандарти ведення трудових книжок періодично змінювалися. Через це відсутність окремих реквізитів не завжди означає втрату стажу — спершу потрібно перевірити вимоги законодавства, які діяли саме на момент внесення конкретного запису.
Відсутня печатка чи підпис у трудовій: чи є ризик втратити стаж
У випадку відсутності у трудовій книжці печатки, підпису або ж інших необхідних відомостей, це ще не означає, що відповідний період роботи не буде врахований під час призначення пенсії.
Відповідно до постанови Кабміну № 637 від 12 серпня 1993 року, яка визначає порядок зарахування трудового стажу для пенсійних виплат, у разі відсутності трудової книжки, помилок чи відсутніх записів уній, підтвердити період роботи можна за допомогою інших офіційних документів.
Залежно від обставин підтвердити періоди роботи можуть допомогти:
- відомості з реєстру застрахованих осіб;
- довідки з підприємств, установ та організацій;
- витяги з наказів про прийняття на роботу та звільнення;
- особові рахунки й відомості про нарахування або виплату заробітної плати;
- письмові трудові договори та угоди з відмітками про їх виконання;
- інші документи, які містять інформацію про періоди роботи.
Перелік необхідних документів залежить від специфіки виявлених помилок у книжці та умов, за яких людина здійснювала трудову діяльність. Саме тому в разі виникнення будь-яких сумнівів варто звернутися за консультацією до Пенсійного фонду України, де підкажуть, якими саме довідками можна підтвердити спірний період роботи.
Що робити, якщо в трудовій книжці виявили помилки
У разі виявлення розбіжностей необхідно ретельно перевірити кожен запис у розділі «Відомості про роботу». Важливо звірити дати зарахування та звільнення, повні назви організацій, зафіксовані посади, а також реквізити відповідних наказів із їхніми номерами й датами.
Якщо компанія свого часу змінила назву, у документі обов’язково має бути запис про таке реорганізування з посиланням на відповідний розпорядчий документ.
Виправляти помилки насамперед має той роботодавець, який їх припустився, або ж його правонаступник у разі реорганізації. У них можна отримати виправлений запис чи необхідні підтверджувальні папери.
Коли ж підприємство вже припинило існування або не зберегло потрібних архівів, варто зв’язатися з Пенсійним фондом для уточнення алгоритму дій. У таких ситуаціях зазвичай запитують архівні довідки та інші передбачені законом документи.
Пенсія в Україні — останні новини
Українським пенсіонерам іноді доводиться підтверджувати розмір пенсії — така довідка потрібна для оформлення пільг, соціальної допомоги, звернення до банку, консульських установ чи інших органів, зокрема за кордоном. Отримати її можна дистанційно, адже Пенсійний фонд України має відповідні дані в державних реєстрах, хоча перелік документів залежить від мети звернення та вимог установи.
Варто зауважити, що від 1 квітня 2026 року частина українських пенсіонерів залишилася без виплат, і найскладніше поновити їх тим, хто перебуває за кордоном або на тимчасово окупованих територіях, адже довідка про неотримання російської пенсії насправді не існує і Пенсійний фонд України її не вимагає. Для відновлення нарахувань достатньо подати до ПФУ заяву-декларацію про те, що пенсія від РФ не отримується, і виплати поновлюються на підставі особистої заяви пенсіонера під його відповідальність.

content:

Навіть дрібні помилки в датах або відсутність однієї печатки в трудовій книжці можуть заблокувати зарахування страхового стажу під час оформлення пенсійних виплат.
При оформленні пенсійних виплат навіть незначні помилки в трудовій книжці часто призводять до додаткових перевірок. Пропущені печатки, відсутність підписів чи помилки в датах суттєво ускладнюють підтвердження страхового стажу.
Необхідно завчасно переглянути свої документи, щоб без поспіху виправити помилки й у разі потреби зібрати необхідні довідки, повідомляє видання «На пенсії».
Що обов’язково треба перевірити в трудовій книжці перед оформленням пенсії
Перш за все варто перевірити першу сторінку трудової книжки, де зазначені особисті дані власника. Важливо переконатися, що прізвище, ім’я та по батькові вказані правильно, а дата народження відповідає даним паспорта або іншого документа, що посвідчує особу.
Також потрібно звернути увагу на оформлення першої сторінки. Відповідно до норм, які діяли під час її заповнення, там обов’язково мають стояти підписи власника та відповідального працівника, а також печатка організації чи кадрового відділу.
Також необхідно ретельно звірити записи про прийняття на роботу та звільнення. Переконайтеся у відсутності помилок у датах, назвах компаній і посадах, а також у тому, що формулювання про звільнення засвідчені належним чином згідно з тогочасними правилами.
При цьому слід враховувати, що стандарти ведення трудових книжок періодично змінювалися. Через це відсутність окремих реквізитів не завжди означає втрату стажу — спершу потрібно перевірити вимоги законодавства, які діяли саме на момент внесення конкретного запису.

У випадку відсутності у трудовій книжці печатки, підпису або ж інших необхідних відомостей, це ще не означає, що відповідний період роботи не буде врахований під час призначення пенсії.
Відповідно до постанови Кабміну № 637 від 12 серпня 1993 року, яка визначає порядок зарахування трудового стажу для пенсійних виплат, у разі відсутності трудової книжки, помилок чи відсутніх записів уній, підтвердити період роботи можна за допомогою інших офіційних документів.

- довідки з підприємств, установ та організацій;

title: Украина получит новую помощь как минимум от пяти стран
content_c:
О предстоящих пакетах поддержки сообщил министр иностранных дел Андрей Сибига.
На сегодняшний день уже пять стран подтвердили предоставление новых пакетов помощи Украине в энергетической, гуманитарной и оборонной сферах. Об этом сообщил министр иностранных дел Андрей Сибига, передает "Укринформ".
«Я уверен, что будут дополнительные энергетические, гуманитарные и оборонные пакеты… У меня есть подтверждение о новых пакетах как минимум от пяти стран. Мы уже знаем, от кого они поступят, сейчас уточняются объемы. И мы получим дополнительную помощь», — отметил глава украинской дипломатии.
Отметим, что президент Владимир Зеленский 15 октября начал визит в Брюссель, где провел встречи с генеральным секретарем НАТО Марком Рютте, премьер-министром Польши Дональдом Туском, президентом Франции Эммануэлем Макроном. Президент также встретился с королём Бельгии Филиппом, премьер-министром Бельгии Бартом де Вевером и премьер-министром Дании Метте Фредериксен.

title: Корецький по результатам онлайн-зустріч з бізнесом: розглядаємо варіанти допомоги в умовах вкрай обмежених фінресурсів
content_c:
Прем'єр-міністр України Сергій Корецький заявляє, що уряд розглядає різні варіанти, як держава може допомогти підприємцям в умовах вкрай обмежених фінансових ресурсів.
"Був відвертий діалог щодо механізмів підтримки підприємців в умовах цілеспрямованих російських ударів по виробництвах, складах тощо. Розглядаємо різні варіанти, як держава може допомогти підприємцям в умовах вкрай обмежених фінансових ресурсів. Почув позицію і аргументи бізнесу. Разом з міністром економіки Олександром Кравченком розповіли про урядові ініціативи", – написав Корецький в телеграм-каналі по результатам онлайн-зустріч з представниками бізнесу.
Також він подякував всім підприємцям, які продовжують працювати, зберігати робочі місця, сплачувати податки.
Як повідомлялося, на початку вересня на тлі посилення російських атак на український бізнес та цивільну інфраструктуру уряд заявив, що готує програму пільгового кредитування на поповнення обігових коштів обсягом до 1 млрд грн для одного підприємства або групи підприємств із компенсацією 5% від ринкової ставки, повідомляв прем'єр-міністр України Сергій Корецький.
Пропозиція Міністерства економіки та довкілля сформувати страховий фонд компенсацій бізнесу втрат від обстрілів за рахунок підвищення ставки податку на додану вартість на 1 відсотковий пункт (в.п.) – до 21% не отримала однозначної підтримки бізнесу, свідчить проведені агентством "Інтерфакс-Україна" опитування близько десятка компаній і бізнес-асоціацій та дискусія у соцмережах.

title: Why is Starlink internet so important on the battlefield in Ukraine?
content_c:
Why is Starlink internet so important on the battlefield in Ukraine?
- Published
Starlink satellites operated by Elon Musk's SpaceX provide high-speed internet - something modern war relies heavily on.
For Ukraine, it is vital for communications on the battlefield and effective drone warfare.
Using Starlink, Ukrainian drones can stay connected to operators over longer distances than conventional radio networks and are less vulnerable to jamming.
But on Tuesday night, Starlink suddenly and unexpectedly restricted the speed at which drones could fly while still maintaining internet connection. This disrupted some battlefield "missions", a top Ukrainian official said, and hampered Kyiv's ability to protect itself from incoming Russian attacks.
The restriction at 100mph (160km/h) meant that any drone travelling faster than that lost connection and was effectively useless.
"Starlink gives Ukraine the ability to see what's coming, to protect people," Kurt Volker, former US ambassador to Nato, told the BBC's Radio 4 Today programme. "If you cut that off, then more people are going to get killed - and that is a very cynical and callous decision to slow that down the way that has been done."
Connectivity had been restored by Wednesday evening.
The move has once again shown how Starlink can impact the conflict, which has been raging since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
What are Starlink and Starshield?
Starlink is an internet network that uses satellites in low Earth orbit to provide connectivity, particularly in remote areas and battlefields.
It currently relies on more than 10,000 active satellites, making Starlink the world's largest satellite constellation.
It is owned by Elon Musk's SpaceX, and is the company's biggest revenue driver.
While Starlink is for civilian use, Starshield is its military-grade sister service, designed for the Pentagon.
Starshield relies on the Starlink network, but has greater security like enhanced encryption so that sensitive information can be transmitted without interception.
The US government has allowed Ukraine to use Starlink and Starshield in its defence against Russia. Musk cut Moscow's access to the service in February, giving Kyiv an advantage in the conflict.
How does Starlink work on a battlefield?
Put simply, Starlink uses its thousands of satellites to ping high-speed internet back to almost every corner of the globe, using terminals on the ground that users can easily buy and set up themselves. As Musk said, they have two instructions: "point at sky, plug in".
This makes them ideal for use on the battlefield.
"It's a connection… that you can basically use pretty fast, you don't need any special equipment, you don't need to prepare, you just go to the field and usually it works," Neo, a soldier with one of Ukraine's drone reconnaissance units, told the Today programme.
"It simplifies our work because we can translate or stream our reconnaissance operations," he added.
The network has become "the backbone of military communications in Ukraine", George Barros from the Institute for the Study of War (ISW) said, and is used across Kyiv's naval, land, and air forces.
In Ukraine, both Starlink (the civilian service) and Starshield (the military service) are used, depending on what communications are needed.
It is crucial for the effective use of weapons such as drones, which connect to the network so that operators can see their targets in real time, effectively minimising the time between "sensor-to shooter", Barros told the BBC.
Because Russia is not authorised to use Starlink, when Ukraine sends long-range missiles deep into Russia to hit oil refineries, the network does not work.
When it comes to Ukraine's self-defence, it relies on the Starlink network to protect its own skies against incoming Russian attacks, especially jet-powered Shahed drones, Barros added.
Shaheds fly at speeds in excess of 198mph (319 km/h), meaning the Starlink restriction made Ukrainian efforts to chase them down all but impossible.
For Neo, this means that any deliberate restrictions on the Starlink network are "a betrayal".
With no ready replacement for the Starlink network, any speed restrictions or loss of connectivity have major implications for Ukraine defences, and the recent limits have shown how dependent Kyiv is on the network.
While Starlink can provide access nearly everywhere in the world, that does not mean it can be accessed everywhere, and countries must be licenced to use it.
Russia is one place where it is not authorised, although Kyiv has in the past said that Moscow was still getting hold of the terminals and using them in occupied territory in Ukraine.
"If SpaceX obtains knowledge that Starlink terminal is being used by a sanctioned or unauthorized party, we investigate the claim and take actions to deactivate the terminal if confirmed," Starlink said in 2024.
But with tens of thousands of terminals in Ukraine alone, it could be a near impossible task to determine which terminals are authorised and which ones are not.
Why did Starlink restrict drone speeds?
The answer remains unclear.
During a visit to London on Wednesday, Zelensky had said he hoped it was just a mistake, however, in a later interview with the Financial Times, he said: "It was not a technical problem, it was the will."
Musk said that Starshield is managed by the US government and suggested the Pentagon could be responsible.
"Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government," he wrote on X, external. "Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS [the president of the United States]."
He added: "Starlink is a commercial service owned and controlled by SpaceX. Usage of Starlink is limited to civilian or defensive activities and cannot be used for offensive military action, as doing so would be inappropriate for a commercial company."
The BBC has contacted the White House and Pentagon for comment.
The restrictions on Tuesday night came as Russia launched deadly attacks against Ukraine that left 600,000 without power and hit communications and energy facilities used by Ukraine's military. Residents said they received no warning of incoming drones before they hit.
"It is clear that this action cannot be a coincidence and is related to the current political situation," Zelensky's adviser Serhiy Beskrestnov wrote on Telegram on Wednesday morning.
Relations between the US and Ukraine have worsened recently, especially since the US announced a deal with Russia to import its diesel into the American market.
Zelensky called it a gift to Russian President Vladimir Putin, and in response Donald Trump said he thinks "it's time for Ukraine to get a new president".
On Sunday, Trump announced a ceasefire on energy infrastructure, but three days later, Ukraine said it would resume the strikes, accusing Russia of ignoring it (the Kremlin said it had never agreed to a ceasefire), and the US of withdrawing crucial support.
Zelensky has accused the US of threatening to withhold intelligence if Ukraine continues striking Russian oil facilities. Trump has denied this, but last week told reporters that Zelensky had "better damn well stop" the strikes.
While in London, Zelensky agreed that he felt betrayed by the US.
Trump's deal with Russia is his administration's latest effort to lower US fuel prices ahead of next month's midterm elections, after months spent grappling with the political consequences of the Iran war. That conflict, which started in February, has seen prices skyrocket, souring his standing with the American public.

title: UK HRT shortages: which products are affected and what to do about it
content_c: Estradot, one of the products affected, is the second longest running individual medicine shortage in the UK. Photograph: Nicola K photos/AlamyView image in fullscreenEstradot, one of the products affected, is the second longest running individual medicine shortage in the UK. Photograph: Nicola K photos/AlamyExplainerUK HRT shortages: which products are affected and what to do about itExperts say seeking alternatives that deliver the same dose of oestrogen by the same method is keyWomen in the UK are again facing shortages of some HRT products, with warnings they could persist for weeks. We take a look at the situation.What is HRT?Hormone replacement therapy is widely used to help women manage symptoms of menopause. It can take many forms, from gels and sprays to patches, pills, creams and intrauterine systems.As the NHS notes, HRT typically involves two hormones – oestrogen and progestogen – and replaces levels lost as women go through menopause. These can be given separately or in a single type of HRT. Women who have had a hysterectomy only require oestrogen-containing HRT.According to the NHS Business Services Authority (NHSBSA), almost 2 million women in England aged 40 and above were prescribed HRT for menopause symptoms in 2025-26. Experts, however, say that access varies and shortages have been a problem.Which items are affected by the current shortages?According to a medicine supply notification issued by the Department of Health and Social Care this week, FemSeven Conti patches are out of stock and are expected to remain so until late November. The patches contain estradiol – a type of oestrogen– and a synthetic progestogen called levonorgestrel.There are also shortages of various Estradot patches – a type of HRT that contains estradiol – and the situation is not expected to end until January.This is not the first time there have been HRT shortages, and the supply issues affecting Estradot have been long-lasting. The shortages of some products began in December 2024, according to NHSBSA.“When you have found an HRT treatment that helps you sleep, manage hot flushes and feel more like yourself, being told it is unavailable can be unsettling,” said Sobia Qasim, a pharmacist at the online pharmacy Curely.Sehar Shahid, a member of the National Pharmacy Association’s board, also raised concerns. “We are deeply frustrated and concerned by shortages to a number of HRT products, with shortages of Estradot being the second longest running individual medicine shortage in the UK,” she said.“Certain HRT products are specialised and cannot always be easily substituted for an alternative.”What alternatives are there?According to the FemSeven Conti notification, alternative patches include Evorel Conti, Estradot Conti 30/95 and Estradot Conti 40/130. These contain estradiol and a different type of synthetic progestogen called norethisterone, and are used twice rather than once a week.Paula Briggs, a consultant in sexual and reproductive health and a former chair of the British Menopause Society, said keeping the same dose of estradiol was the important aspect. “They have different progestogens, but I do not think that that would have any adverse impact on symptom control,” she said, noting progestogens are required to protect the lining of the womb rather than manage symptoms.Serious shortage protocols for the Estradot products also list alternatives, such as estradiol-containing patches by Estraderm MX and Evorel. “If we’re using the same dose of oestrogen delivered in a similar patch through the skin, really there is no need to worry,” said Briggs.What should women do if they are affected by the shortages?Shahid said people who had experienced disruption to their usual HRT regime should speak to their clinician, while Qasim cautioned against leaving a patch on for longer than prescribed, cutting patches up or borrowing HRT treatments from others.What needs to happen next?Briggs said shortages were likely to occur in the future “because year on year we’re seeing a more than 10% increase in use”, she said.Shahid urged the government to take action. “The new secretary of state should convene a taskforce to fully grasp this issue, bringing together all aspects of the supply chain,” she said.Explore more on these topicsMenopauseWomen's healthNHSHealthDrugsPharmaceuticals industrynewsShareReuse this content

title: Why Chinese tech brands are outpacing Western rivals from EVs to robot vacuums
content_c:
How China came to dominate consumer technology
October 15, 2026
Do you remember the days when GoPro was synonymous with action cameras?
At its peak in 2015, the US company reigned supreme with around 6.6 million units sold that year and a market share of over 70%. Today, the pioneer is fighting for survival.
The main culprit? Chinese competition.
GoPro's biggest rivals, DJI and Insta360, entered the action camera market in 2019 and 2021, respectively. Today, they account for more than 90% of global smart handheld camera sales.
Alexander Hannemann, who regularly uses action cameras to film his motorcycle rides, says he switched from GoPro to Insta360 around two years ago.
"The quality is much better than a GoPro, even when I'm speeding up and going into corners at like 80 kilometers per hour," he told DW.
China's growing tech lead
GoPro's case is not an exception. Since around 2010, many Chinese brands have not only caught up but surpassed once-dominant Western rivals across the consumer technology industry, from smart TVs to robot vacuums.
Gone are the days when "Made in China" stood for cheap, mass-produced products.
"China is still making affordable products today," says Chris Pereira, a Canadian entrepreneur and author with over 20 years of experience in China. "But the products are also high quality."
This combination has led to well over half of new consumer tech products globally coming from Chinese suppliers, Pereira adds.
BYD, Xpeng and other Chinese car manufactures sold almost two-thirds of all electric cars last year, surpassing incumbents like Tesla. In robot vacuums, Chinese brands dominate the global market, leaving former pioneer US company iRobot struggling to compete.
So why do Chinese companies increasingly outperform their Western rivals?
Pereira, whose consultancy iMpact helps Chinese companies gain traction overseas, attributes China's success to fierce domestic competition in cities like Shenzhen, Hangzhou and Shanghai; highly integrated supply chains and a can-do business culture that allows companies to innovate; and respond to problems quickly.
Other key reasons for China's competitive edge include unparalleled industrial automation, the strategic use of AI in manufacturing, responsiveness from regulators as well as relatively cheap labor, which together leads to significantly lower production costs and much faster innovation cycles than in the world's most advanced economies.
Joey Cheng, who moved to the US for his PhD studies over 20 years ago, is familiar with both the American consumer and the Chinese producer sides.
While his startup is based in the US, almost all the manufacturing is done in Shenzhen, where a large share of the world's hardware and consumer electronics are made.
"The supply chain in Shenzhen is basically inevitable for cost cutting and quick product development," Cheng says. "Especially as a startup you must get the product out quickly, or you'll get blown out of the water."
Privacy and security concerns persist
Although consumers are flocking to Chinese companies, some reservations persist.
A recent poll found that more than 90% of Europeans do not trust Chinese technology companies with their data, while about 80% distrust US firms. Germans expressed the highest level of mistrust.
Nadine, a German travel blogger who uses DJI and Insta360 products, says she wouldn't use any Asian products at home.
"My home robot vacuum is from a German company for precisely this reason: So the data remains compliant with German regulations. After all, manufacturers can connect directly to the camera," she said, referring to camera and audio hacking incidents involving robot vacuums.
Still, Pereira says that Chinese companies expanding abroad have to pay a "trust premium."
"This trust deficit means that they need to be extra competitive in terms of product and price in order for the market to choose them," he says, adding that the gap can be narrowed by a presence in overseas markets like BYD's first European passenger-car plant, expected to open in Hungary later this year.
Chinese companies say they comply with EU data protection rules. However, domestic security laws in the US and China can require firms to hand over data to authorities, and German officials note limited oversight of whether data is transferred from European servers abroad.
In addition to privacy concerns, Chinese consumer tech firms have come under scrutiny over espionage and other risks, most recently regarding connected devices like EVs.
Is a new trade war brewing?
In light of security concerns, trade deficits and China's overall dominance, the US and several other Western countries have hit Chinese imports and companies with tariffs, blacklists and strict requirements. In late July, the Trump administration banned the import of humanoid robots manufactured outside the US.
A representative of Chinese robot maker Primebot told DW that all Chinese consumer tech companies are feeling the effects.
"We might seek cooperation with a local US company. Another potential solution is building a factory there," he said.
European countries and the EU are also weighing more tariffs against Chinese companies.
Chris Pereira foresees that the tariffs will accelerate two trends among Chinese companies: Moving more manufacturing overseas and an increasing focus on challenging top-tier Western brands with premium goods.
"Chinese officials and companies recognize that manufacturing needs to be localized to a certain degree. One reason is to assuage the challenges of exporting, another is to create trust locally," Pereira sums up.
"The other trend is that once duties wipe out the price advantage at the bottom, the margin left is at the top, so Chinese brands are increasingly competing directly with established Western names, where trust matters most."
Can Western companies compete?
As China's dominance keeps growing, Western companies are scrambling to find ways to stay competitive.
Kaz Merchant, who works for a UK-based company that imports and exports IT hardware, says smaller companies, in particular, must carve out a geographic niche.
"They need to have their own unique selling point for a certain product, which China might not have for that region. Or they need to partner with a Chinese company," he says.
To Pereira, a key issue Europe needs to solve is regulators' responsiveness.
"Chinese regulators tell you very clearly and quickly what you can do. That speed helps companies iterate and succeed overseas," Pereira says.
"If you're waiting weeks for a response, you're going to lose business."
Edited by: Tim Rooks

"The supply chain in Shenzhen is basically inevitable for cost cutting and quick product development," Cheng says. "Especially as a startup you must get the product out quickly, or you'll get blown out of the water."
Privacy and security concerns persist
Although consumers are flocking to Chinese companies, some reservations persist.
A recent poll found that more than 90% of Europeans do not trust Chinese technology companies with their data, while about 80% distrust US firms. Germans expressed the highest level of mistrust.
Nadine, a German travel blogger who uses DJI and Insta360 products, says she wouldn't use any Asian products at home.
"My home robot vacuum is from a German company for precisely this reason: So the data remains compliant with German regulations. After all, manufacturers can connect directly to the camera," she said, referring to camera and audio hacking incidents involving robot vacuums.
Still, Pereira says that Chinese companies expanding abroad have to pay a "trust premium."
"This trust deficit means that they need to be extra competitive in terms of product and price in order for the market to choose them," he says, adding that the gap can be narrowed by a presence in overseas markets like BYD's first European passenger-car plant, expected to open in Hungary later this year.
Chinese companies say they comply with EU data protection rules. However, domestic security laws in the US and China can require firms to hand over data to authorities, and German officials note limited oversight of whether data is transferred from European servers abroad.
In addition to privacy concerns, Chinese consumer tech firms have come under scrutiny over espionage and other risks, most recently regarding connected devices like EVs.
Is a new trade war brewing?
In light of security concerns, trade deficits and China's overall dominance, the US and several other Western countries have hit Chinese imports and companies with tariffs, blacklists and strict requirements. In late July, the Trump administration banned the import of humanoid robots manufactured outside the US.
A representative of Chinese robot maker Primebot told DW that all Chinese consumer tech companies are feeling the effects.
"We might seek cooperation with a local US company. Another potential solution is building a factory there," he said.
European countries and the EU are also weighing more tariffs against Chinese companies.
Chris Pereira foresees that the tariffs will accelerate two trends among Chinese companies: Moving more manufacturing overseas and an increasing focus on challenging top-tier Western brands with premium goods.
"Chinese officials and companies recognize that manufacturing needs to be localized to a certain degree. One reason is to assuage the challenges of exporting, another is to create trust locally," Pereira sums up.
"The other trend is that once duties wipe out the price advantage at the bottom, the margin left is at the top, so Chinese brands are increasingly competing directly with established Western names, where trust matters most."
Can Western companies compete?
As China's dominance keeps growing, Western companies are scrambling to find ways to stay competitive.
Kaz Merchant, who works for a UK-based company that imports and exports IT hardware, says smaller companies, in particular, must carve out a geographic niche.
"They need to have their own unique selling point for a certain product, which China might not have for that region. Or they need to partner with a Chinese company," he says.
To Pereira, a key issue Europe needs to solve is regulators' responsiveness.
"Chinese regulators tell you very clearly and quickly what you can do. That speed helps companies iterate and succeed overseas," Pereira says.
"If you're waiting weeks for a response, you're going to lose business."
Edited by: Tim Rooks

title: Zeitmessung: Schaltsekunde wird abgeschafft – wegen Gefahr einer Minus-Schaltsekunde
content_c:
Zeitmessung Schaltsekunde wird abgeschafft
Die Generalkonferenz für Maß und Gewicht (CGPM) hat in Versailles bei Paris entschieden, dass ab dem 20. Mai 2027 eine fortlaufende Koordinierte Weltzeit (UTC) gelten soll. Damit wird die Schaltsekunde abgeschafft. Bisher wurde diese in unregelmäßigen Abständen eingefügt, um unsere Uhren mit der astronomischen Zeit in Einklang zu halten. Grund für die Entscheidung ist unter anderem die Angst vor den Auswirkungen von Schaltsekunden auf die immer sensibleren IT-Systeme.
Bei der Zeitmessung gibt es zwei verschiedene Grundlagen. Die UTC basiert auf der Messung von Atomuhren. Die astronomische Zeit (UT1, Universalzeit) wird durch die Erdrotation bestimmt. Atomuhren liefern eine konstante Zeit, während die Rotationsgeschwindigkeit der Erde geringfügig schwankt. Das führt dazu, dass die beiden Zeitskalen immer wieder leicht voneinander abweichen.
Um die Zeiten möglichst gleich zu halten, galt bisher, dass UTC und UT1 maximal 0,9 Sekunden voneinander abweichen dürfen. War die Differenz erreicht, wurde eine Schaltsekunde eingefügt. Seit der Einführung des Verfahrens 1972 ist das genau 27-mal geschehen, zuletzt 2016. Entschieden wurde vom Internationalen Erdrotations- und Referenzsystemdienst (IERS). Die zusätzliche Sekunde wurde entweder am Ende des 30. Juni oder des 31. Dezember eingeschoben. Die entsprechende Minute hatte dann 61 statt der üblichen 60 Sekunden.
Bald ist eine Abweichung von bis zu einer Stunde erlaubt
Künftig soll die Koordinierte Weltzeit nach Entscheidung der Generalkonferenz bis zu 3600 Sekunden und damit eine ganze Stunde von der astronomischen Zeit abweichen dürfen. Die Fachleute hoffen, dass die Zeiterfassung so für mehrere Jahrhunderte nicht angepasst werden muss. Die Konferenz hat sich für diesen Schritt entschieden, weil die Sekunde für Menschen zwar meist unbemerkt bleibt, in Computersystemen aber Störungen verursachen kann. Auch kritische Infrastruktur wie Energieversorgung, Telekommunikation oder Verkehr braucht laut CGPM eine konstante Zeit ohne Anpassungen.
Schon in der Vergangenheit war über ein Aus der Schaltsekunde diskutiert worden. Dass die CGPM sich nun schon früher als einst angedacht für diesen Schritt entschied, liegt auch an einer sonst möglicherweise notwendigen Minus-Schaltsekunde, da die Erdrotation sich zuletzt verändert hat. Über sehr lange Zeiträume wird diese durch Gezeitenkräfte von Mond und Sonne gebremst. In den vergangenen Jahren allerdings hat sich die Erdrotation laut CGPM leicht beschleunigt.
Laut Fachleuten bestand dadurch die Möglichkeit, dass erstmals eine Sekunde abgezogen und nicht hinzugefügt werden müsste, um UTC und UT1 wieder anzugleichen. Ob der Abzug der Sekunde störungsfrei umgesetzt werden könnte, war unklar. Die Industrie befürchtete der CGPM zufolge erhebliche technische Vorbereitungen und zusätzliche Kosten.
- 
2 Min
- 
2 Min
Mit der Abschaffung der Schaltsekunde werden sich UTC und UT1 nach und nach weiter voneinander entfernen. Die Uhrzeit würde stärker vom Stand der Sonne am Himmel abweichen, was im Alltag noch für lange Zeit bedeutungslos sein dürfte. Auswirkungen könnte die Änderung vor allem für diejenigen haben, die mit der astronomischen Zeit arbeiten – etwa Astronomen oder Fachleute der Geodäsie, der Vermessung der Erdoberfläche.

title: Marktbericht: TSMC gibt sich keine Blöße
content_c:
Erneut mit Rekordgewinn TSMC zeigt weiter keine Schwäche
Neue US-Zinssorgen drücken vor allem die Kurse der hochbewerteten Tech-Aktien, allen voran der Chiphersteller. Die Fakten sprechen aber eine andere Sprache - wie heute die Zahlen von TSMC zeigen.
Der KI-Boom scheint nicht zu enden - ob Nvidia, Samsung oder gestern die beeindruckenden Zahlen des Chipausrüsters ASML, egal wo die Unternehmen in der KI-Wertschöpfungskette stehen, ein Rekordergebnis jagt derzeit das andere.
Denn die Nachfrage kann das Angebot weiterhin nicht abdecken. Aber kann das ewig so weitergehen? An der Börse häufen sich die Zweifel, auch wenn die nackten Zahlen diese Ängste weiterhin nicht bestätigen.
TSMC: Weiteres Rekordergebnis
So hatte der taiwanische Chip-Auftragsfertiger TSMC bereits vergangene Woche einen Umsatzsprung von 50 Prozent auf einen Höchststand von 41,66 Milliarden Euro bekanntgegeben und erklärt, dass vorerst kein Ende dieser Entwicklung in Sicht sei. Für das laufende Quartal stellte das Unternehmen eine Beschleunigung des Wachstums auf 55 bis 61 Prozent in Aussicht. Außerdem präzisierte es seine Gesamtjahresziele. Der Umsatz werde voraussichtlich um 44 Prozent steigen.
Heute nun veröffentlichte TSMC seine Gewinnzahlen, die entsprechend beeindruckend ausfielen - mit einem Gewinn im Quartal von umgerechnet rund 21 Milliarden Euro. Laut dem US-Finanzdienst CNBC war es das sechste Rekordquartal beim Gewinn für TSMC in Folge.
Der hohen Nachfrage kommt der Chip-Auftragsfertiger kaum hinterher. "Daher arbeiten wir mit aller Kraft am Ausbau unserer Produktionskapazitäten", teilte TSMC mit. Der Konzern bestätigte sein Investitionsziel für 2026 von 64 Milliarden Dollar, was die nervösen Anleger etwas beruhigte. Normale Industriebetriebe können von solchen Zahlen nur träumen.
TSMC ist der weltweit größte Auftragshersteller von Halbleitern. Mit dem massiven Ausbau der Rechenzentrumskapazitäten weltweit wegen des großen Bedarfs durch KI ist die Nachfrage nach Chips stark gestiegen.
Zinsängste im Fokus
Bei Anlegern im Technologiesektor geht trotzdem die Angst um. Denn die Furcht vor höheren Zinsen nimmt nach den jüngsten, hohen US-Inflationszahlen zu. Gerade Tech-Unternehmen sind aber stark finanzierungsabhängig.
"Die Aufnahme von Krediten zu sehr hohen Zinssätzen, um Rechenzentren zu errichten, die außerhalb der Hyperscaler zunehmend zu einer Massenware werden, könnte sich letztlich als keine gute Investition erweisen", äußerte sich Analyst Gil Luria von D.A. Davidson skeptisch. Je mehr Fremdkapital wir für den Bau von Rechenzentren einsetzen, desto mehr Risiko bringen wir in das System ein."
Deutlicher Abverkauf
Wie nervös die Anleger wegen der höheren Zinserwartungen derzeit sind, haben der deutliche Rückgang der US-Technologiebörse Nasdaq am Vortag, sowie der heutige Börsentag in Asien gezeigt. Besonders stark waren die Verluste in Südkorea, wo der Leitindex Kospi um rund neun Prozent einbrach. Der ebenfalls technologielastige japanische Nikkei-Index gab um fast fünf Prozent nach. Die Börse Shanghai und der Index der wichtigsten Unternehmen in Shanghai und Shenzhen büßten jeweils gut zwei Prozent ein.
"Anleger zweifeln nicht an der Nachfrage nach KI", sagte Charu Chanana, Anlagestrategin bei der Saxo Bank. "Sie fragen sich zunehmend, welchen Preis sie für dieses Wachstum zahlen sollten, wenn die Zinsen hoch sind und möglicherweise weiter steigen."
DAX etwas schwächer - Infineon und Siemens Energy brechen ein
Der Tech-Ausverkauf in Übersee belastet auch den DAX, der am frühen Nachmittag rund 0,4 Prozent nachgibt.
Selbst die überraschend starken Ergebnisse des taiwanischen Halbleiterkonzerns TSMC hätten die Anleger nicht beruhigt, sagte Andreas Lipkow, Chefanalyst beim Broker CMC Markets. "Wenn selbst gute Nachrichten nicht mehr gekauft werden, sondern zum Ausstieg genutzt werden, ist das ein deutliches Warnsignal für die Börsen."
Größter Verlierer im DAX sind Chiphersteller Infineon und Siemens Energy. Die ehemalige Siemens-Sparte gilt mit ihrer Netzsparte als Profiteur beim Bau von Rechenzentren.

title: Руководитель BlackRock предупредил о нехватке средств на развитие ИИ
content_c:
Председатель совета директоров и генеральный директор крупнейшей в мире компании по управлению активами BlackRock Ларри Финк заявил, что за полвека работы впервые сталкивается с реальной нехваткой финансирования. Только США требуется от 7 до 9 трлн долларов на инфраструктуру для искусственного интеллекта: дата-центры, электросети и энергоснабжение. Из-за таких масштабов Финк ожидает, что процентные ставки, особенно долгосрочные, будут оставаться высокими еще долго, сообщает Business Insider.
«Впервые за всю мою карьеру, а я работаю 50 лет, я вижу настоящий дефицит капитала», — сказал Финк во время презентации результатов BlackRock за третий квартал. На 30 сентября компания управляла активами на сумму 15,5 трлн долларов, а чистые поступления за квартал составили 205 млрд долларов.
По словам Финка, деньги нужны не только на чипы. Дата-центр мощностью один гигаватт стоит около 50 млрд долларов. Примерно 40% этой суммы приходится на графические процессоры и чипы, остальные 60% уходят на энергию, сети, здания и оборудование.
Высокую стоимость денег Финк связывает с масштабом потребностей: государствам тоже требуется значительное финансирование, поэтому за капитал приходится конкурировать. «У нас будут структурно более высокие процентные ставки в течение значительно более длительного времени, особенно на длинном конце кривой доходности», — предупредил он.
В BlackRock видят в этом возможность для бизнеса на частных рынках. «Создание нового механизма финансирования вычислительных мощностей и чипов является насущной необходимостью», — подчеркнул Финк.
BlackRock уже работает над проектами в этой сфере: дата-центром в Техасе совместно с Meta стоимостью около 14 млрд долларов и сделкой по Aligned Data Centers, корпоративная стоимость которой составляет около 40 млрд долларов.
Финк также предостерег от концентрации ресурсов. «Мы не можем допустить, чтобы всего пять или семь компаний скупали все производимые в настоящее время чипы», — сказал он. Выход, по его словам, заключается в расширении каналов финансирования и привлечении частного капитала.
Риски финансирования бума ИИ замечают и центральные банки. В июне Банк международных расчетов предупредил, что финансирование бума искусственного интеллекта все больше опирается на долги и сложные финансовые структуры. О том, почему ФРС держит ставки на высоком уровне и когда их начнут снижать, в статье ZN.UA «Ставки вверх до 2027-го, вниз только с 2028-го: что ФРС готовит мировой экономике» пишет экономист и финансовый аналитик Алексей Кущ.

content:

title: Кабмін призначив Чепурного заступником глави МОЗ, головним санлікарем
content_c:
Кабінет міністрів України призначив Олександра Чепурного заступником міністра охорони здоров'я України, головним державним санітарним лікарем України.
Як повідомив представник Кабміну у Верховній Раді Тарас Мельничук у телеграм-каналі, відповідне рішення ухвалено на засіданні уряду.
Чепурний є генеральним директором Чернігівського обласного центру контролю та профілактики хвороб МОЗ України та головним державним санітарним лікарем Чернігівської області.
В той же час, Ігоря Кузіна звільнено з посади заступника міністра охорони здоров'я – головного держсанлікаря.
Також Ігоря Ільченка призначено головою Національної соціальної сервісної служби України, до цього він обіймав посаду першого заступника.

title: Was Neanderthal life violent? This wound suggests lethal fighting was more common
content_c:
Was Neanderthal life violent? This wound suggests lethal fighting was more common
- Published
A Neanderthal who died 75,000 years ago may have been struck through the chest by a sharpened wooden spear, archaeologists say.
They say a 15mm hole found in a shoulder blade in a cave in Iraqi Kurdistan could be the earliest evidence of lethal violence involving such a weapon.
From the angle of the wound and other evidence, the researchers believe the spear entered the individual's chest and passed through the body - probably damaging a lung and major blood vessels - and exited through the left shoulder blade to leave a near-perfect hole.
The research is the latest in emerging evidence that suggests Neanderthal societies experienced more violence than previously thought.
Neanderthals were a separate species of humans that went extinct around 40,000 years ago. They lived across a large expanse of Europe and western and central Asia, and sometimes overlapped with our species, Homo sapiens.
The wounded Neanderthal's remains were found in a cave in Iraqi Kurdistan. As well as the left shoulder blade, the individual's right hand, three ribs and some teeth were also found.
A hole in the shoulder blade may be the earliest evidence of "lethal interpersonal violence" from a wooden spear, according to Dr Emma Pomeroy, study lead author from Cambridge's Department of Archaeology.
"The fatal strike may have been an intended heart shot," she told BBC News.
Archaeologists call the remains Shanidar A, named after the cave in which they were found. Remains of at least 10 Neanderthals were discovered in excavations in the cave in the 1950s.
The wound is thought to be the first evidence for use of sharpened wooden spears in the prehistoric Middle East, according to Pomeroy.
"It is not the kind of break that you would get naturally, because it is so circular," she said. "Experiments with reconstructed wooden spears produce very similar round holes in bone."
But the interpersonal violence is by no means certain, she says. It may be a case of friendly fire, a wound caused as a result of a hunting accident.
But Prof Chris Stringer of the Natural History Museum in London, who was not involved in the research, told BBC News that an attack by a rival was the more plausible explanation.
"The researchers leave it open whether this resulted from a hunting accident or interpersonal violence, but in my view the latter seems more likely, given the positioning and extent of the wound," he said.
This discovery has echoes of an earlier find in the same cave, in 1957. Those remains involved another Neanderthal who lived more recently, around 50, 000 years ago. Their ribs had evidence of a partly healed wound, which archaeologists believe was probably caused by a stone-tipped spear.
We can't tell for sure whether these Neanderthals were hurt by a companion during a hunt or murdered by a rival. But they join a small but growing body of evidence which point to the possibility that human-on-human violence was more common and goes back further than the current scientific consensus would suggest.
"I unfortunately see the growing body of evidence as an indication that interpersonal violence goes deep into human prehistory," Stringer told BBC News.
A key piece of that evidence is a study published in 2022 of very early Neanderthal skulls from northern Spain at an archaeological site called "the Pit of Bones". It suggests that deadly violence was taking place about 430,000 years ago.
Researchers found 57 healed head injuries among 20 individuals. Nine individuals had potentially fatal skull fractures. Six had similar puncture wounds at the back-left of the head. Because the wounds repeatedly occurred in almost the same place, the researchers concluded that deliberate blows were more likely than accidental damage. One skull had two wounds that had probably been inflicted with the same object.
The Pit of Bones findings do not show that everyone in this population was habitually violent, but they provide strong evidence that repeated killing occurred among these people hundreds of thousands of years ago.
For decades, many archaeologists linked the beginnings of organised warfare to farming, when people began living in permanent settlements and competing over land, livestock and food stores.
But evidence from earlier hunter-gatherers and still older human relatives has since shown that individual killings pre-date farming by a very long way.
The live scientific debate is over how common such violence was, and when sporadic attacks became organised conflict and wars between groups.
The research has been published in the journal Scientific Reports.
